title: [Bugfix][Quark] Honor layer_quant_config for identity packed_modules_mapping entries
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Addresses the identity-entry resolution reported in #54641 by @stefanskiasan. (The
`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` checkpoint that surfaced it needs #56176 instead — see *Scope*.)

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` (a module mapped to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]`) silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config`, so a mixed-precision Quark checkpoint that names the
module is built with the wrong scheme and only fails later, at weight load, with a shape mismatch.

Identity entries exist because the checkpoint really stores the fused tensor: GLM-4.1V ships a
pre-fused `gate_up_proj`, which is why `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration` maps it to itself. A Quark
checkpoint of such a model keys `layer_quant_config` by that fused name, and today that entry is
ignored.

**Scope.** This does *not* fix `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: that config keys the split
`gate_proj` / `up_proj` names (none `gate_up_proj`), and the actual bug there is the identity
mapping `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` inherits from GLM-4.1V although GLM-5.3-Flash stores
gate/up separately — fixed by the mapping override in #56176. Once the mapping expands to real
shards, the branch this PR changes is not reached; the two are complementary. The reporter's
locally produced config named the fused module (the trace in #54641 shows the key present but
`hit=False`), which is exactly the path fixed here.

Both lookup paths in `QuarkConfig` treat `shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None              # identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:
    config = fallback_config   # identity entry -> global scheme
```

That guard is only there to stop the recursion, since substituting an identity entry is a no-op.

title: [CI/Build] Broaden qwen, llama and minimax label rules
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`label-qwen`, `label-llama` and `label-minimax` enumerate directory-and-extension
patterns, so files for those models living anywhere else get no label:

| rule | matched before | of | coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label-qwen` | 83 | 248 | 33% |
| `label-llama` | 16 | 58 | 27% |
| `label-minimax` | 44 | 61 | 72% |

The rules predate several source trees (the Rust frontend, `vllm/tokenizers/`,
`vllm/parser/`, `vllm/renderers/`) and their `\.py` suffixes exclude the `.yaml`
eval configs, `.rs` sources, `.jinja` templates and text fixtures. Qwen is the
worst affected in absolute terms — 165 unlabeled files, most of them under
`tests/evals/`.

## Changes

Replace the enumerations with a single case-insensitive path match, the form
`label-kimi` and `label-rust` already use:

```yaml
- files~=(?i)qwen
- files~=(?i)minimax
- files~=(?i)llama(?!(?:index|stack))
```

All three reach 100% coverage, with zero paths matched that do not name the model.

`llama` needs the exclusion because LlamaIndex and LlamaStack are separate
projects rather than Llama the model; it correctly skips all three such paths
(`docs/deployment/integrations/llamastack.md`,
`docs/serving/integrations/llamaindex.md`, and the LlamaIndex RAG example).

## One judgement call to confirm

The broadened `qwen` pattern now also matches the 8 `colqwen3*` paths
(`vllm/model_executor/models/colqwen3.py` and friends). ColQwen is a
Qwen-derived retrieval model, so labeling it `qwen` seems right to me — but if
you would rather it stay unlabeled, say so and I will add
`(?i)(?<!col)qwen`.

## Deliberately not included

`glm`, `gpt-oss` and `cohere` are left alone. `glm` in particular must not be
broadened this way: `midashenglm.py` is an unrelated model containing the
substring, which is what the existing comment on that rule already guards
against.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --state open --search "mergify label"` returns nothing touching label
configuration. #56332 (`label-dsv4`/`label-dsv4

`vllm/tokenizers/`, `vllm/parser/`, `vllm/renderers/`), and the `\.py` suffixes

## Change

Replace the seven patterns with one:

```yaml
- files~=(?i)deepseek

This is the form `label-kimi` and `label-rust` already use, and it is the reason
`label-kimi` is the only model rule with complete coverage.

Coverage goes from 135/225 to 225/225, with zero non-DeepSeek paths matched.

`gh pr list --state open --search "mergify label"` and `--search "deepseek label"`
return nothing touching label configuration. #56332 (open) edits `label-dsv4` and
adds `label-dsv4-1` in the same file but does not touch `label-deepseek`; the two
do not conflict.

## Testing

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml
```

Passes, including `check-label-rules`.

Coverage measured directly against `git ls-files`, comparing the old seven
patterns with the new one over all 225 tracked paths containing "deepseek":
135 -> 225 matched, and 0 paths without "deepseek" matched by the new condition.

title: [WIP][Bugfix][HiSparse] Restore host mirror state before FULL CUDA graph replay
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix missing host KV writes during HiSparse FULL CUDA graph decode. Once GPU-resident pages are spilled, subsequent host fetches can read unwritten KV and corrupt generation without raising a serving error.

WIP, targeting `feat/hisparse-metrics` (#53782). This contains only the mirror-state correction, a guard against silently missing mirror metadata, and one regression test. CUDA graphs and async scheduling remain enabled.

## Reproduction and cause

We reproduced the issue with GLM-5.3 on two nodes / 16 H200 GPUs, EP16/TP1, using 1,024 concurrent fresh generations from 32 frozen long-reasoning math prompts. The configuration used FP8 KV, 4,096 hot rows, eager host mirroring, a 160 GiB host KV pool per rank, FULL decode graphs, async scheduling, and prefix caching disabled.

Output was initially readable. Resident KV reached capacity around 13.2k median context, and unrelated numeric-word garbling appeared around 13.9k as decoding began relying on host fetches. This happened without client errors or preemptions.

The connector clears per-batch mirror metadata at the beginning of each step. Eager execution rebuilds it in the Python attention path, but FULL graph replay bypasses that Python preparation. Newly written decode KV can therefore be left uncopied on the host. Later spills under eager mirroring trust the host copy, so the problem becomes visible only when those rows are fetched again.

The smaller regression isolates that missing write without a long benchmark: a dummy-weight sparse-MLA model performs FULL-graph decode with eager mirroring and async scheduling, then compares the final decoded token's host KV bytes with its resident GPU bytes. On the original implementation the host row is zero while the GPU row is nonzero.

## Change

- Prepare each HiSparse index-sharing group's per-batch mirror state after `kv_connector.pre_forward()` and before `run_fullgraph()` for real HiSparse batches.
- Raise an error when mirror completion has scheduled

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Route NoPE FP8 KV sparse MLA to Triton instead of AITER asm
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on a rope-free (NoPE) MLA model memory-faults every TP rank during warmup on gfx950. The server never reaches `Application startup complete`.

AITER's precompiled `mla_a8w8` kernels bake in the DeepSeek MLA row width of 576 bytes (512 latent + 64 RoPE) — `0x240` appears as an immediate in the HSACO, and the kernel loads `stride_Q` into `s70` and never uses it. GLM-5.3-Flash has `qk_rope_head_dim=0` and `kv_lora_rank=512`, so its row is 512 bytes. The host computes the correct strides (`stride_Q=8192`, `stride_Page=512`), but the kernel walks 576-byte rows anyway:

- Q overruns by 1024 B per token (8 tokens → +8 KiB, 16 → +16 KiB).
- KV issues 9 unpredicated 64-byte loads covering `[0,576)`; the last 64 B is a phantom RoPE tail, so the final slot reads past the page-aligned cache.

Those offsets match the observed faults: the four ranks faulted at +0, +8 KiB, +16 KiB and +16 KiB past the end of one of their own allocations — a bounded overrun, not a wild pointer.

The routing gate `_use_rocm_sparse_triton` excluded `kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8")`, so BF16 NoPE went to the geometry-parameterized Triton kernel (which loads zero `mla_a8w8` kernels and does not fault) while FP8 NoPE was forced onto the asm kernel.

Fix:

1. Stop gating the rope-free Triton route on the KV dtype.
2. Keep the query in the model dtype on that route (the FP8 quantization exists only for the asm kernel).
3. Dequantize FP8 KV inside the Triton kernel using `layer._k_scale_float`, which is the exact inverse of the `x / k_scale` performed by `concat_and_cache_mla`.
4. Raise `NotImplementedError` for any NoPE row that would still reach the asm kernels. Speculative decode / MTP raises the reorder-batch threshold above 1, which makes the plain-decode predicate false and would otherwise drop NoPE back onto the 576-byte kernel with the same overrun. A clear error beats a memory fault; a shape guard on the ROCm lane was also requested independently in #53963.

title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3 P/D on GB200 — NIXL issues up to ~112k KV descriptors per rank-transfer, making MNNVL/cuda_ipc slower than RDMA on this workload
bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Serving **GLM-5.3** (DeepSeek-V3.2 architecture: MLA + DSA indexer) with P/D disaggregation on GB200, NIXL KV transfer is dominated by **descriptor submission, not fabric bandwidth**. Under agentic load we observe **91,000–120,000 descriptors per TP-rank transfer** for a ~4.9 GB payload, and `cuda_ipc` spends **56.9% of transfer time posting them**.

The consequence: **for this workload shape, the documented GB-series MNNVL configuration is slower end to end than plain RDMA on the same hardware**, because `cuda_ipc` submission costs ~20× more per descriptor than `rc_x`. This is a statement about fragmented, descriptor-heavy transfers, not about the fabrics in general — with few descriptors we would expect MNNVL to win, and its post-submission movement rate is already the equal of IB's.

Descriptor count is not fixed by the model — it is the product of an architectural amplifier and workload-driven fragmentation. Measured below.

### Measurements

GLM-5.3 (NVFP4), DEP8 prefill + TP4 decode, AgentX C64. Deltas from vLLM's NIXL Prometheus histograms over each profile window. `postDuration` is synchronous submission; `xferDuration` is posting plus asynchronous movement/completion.

| Transport | Descriptors / transfer | Post mean | Total mean | Movement remainder | Payload / remainder | Post share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| RoCE `rc_x`, 1 rail | 91,262 | 32.1 ms | 517.4 ms | 485.2 ms | 6.45 GB/s | 6.2% |
| MNNVL `cuda_ipc` | 112,092 | **455.9 ms** | 800.8 ms | 345.0 ms | 14.16 GB/s | **56.9%** |
| Native IB `rc_x`, 4 rails | 119,984 | 24.4 ms | 350.8 ms | 326.4 ms | 15.11 GB/s | 7.0% |

Amortized submission cost per descriptor: `rc_x` IB **0.204 µs**, `rc_x` RoCE **0.352 µs**, `cuda_ipc` **4.067 µs**.

Two things to note:

- IB posted **more** descriptors than MNNVL and did it **18.7× faster**. The descriptor geometry was *comparable*, not identical (119,984 vs 112,092, within 7%), so the difference is in the submission

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Poolside: stray arg_key tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`PoolsideV1ToolParser.func_arg_regex` captures the argument key with a plain
`.*?`:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>(.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>", re.DOTALL
)
```

A non-greedy `.*?` guarantees only the *shortest match consistent with the
rest of the pattern*, not that it stops at the first literal `</arg_key>`.
If `\s*<arg_value>` fails to match right after that first occurrence, the
engine backtracks and lets `.*?` cross the boundary to reach a *later*
`</arg_key>`, silently absorbing a stray `<arg_key>`/`</arg_key>` tag into
the parsed key.

This is the identical defect class and identical fix shape as the GLM-4.7
leak fixed in #54971 (reviewer Manny7717 flagged this exact call site in
that PR's review, at `vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py:82`).
The fix bounds the key to runs of non-`<` text, so the capture group can
never cross its own delimiter:

```python
self.func_arg_regex = re.compile(
    r"<arg_key>([^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
    r"<arg_value>(.*?)</arg_value>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

This file uses the third-party `regex` module (`import regex as re`), not
stdlib `re` — `regex` has always supported possessive quantifiers (`*+`)
regardless of interpreter version, so (unlike a stdlib-`re` site) no
non-possessive fallback is needed here. The repo's `requires-python` floor
is `>=3.10,<3.15`; the dev venv used for testing runs 3.13.15, and a
20,000-case randomized differential check (see Test Result) against the
old pattern found no divergence on well-formed input and no leaked `<` in
malformed input.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs against `poolside`/`arg_key`/`tool_parsers` before
starting. The only overlapping PR is #54678
("[Bugfix][Security] Fix catastrophic backtracking in the poolside_v1 and
dots tool-call regexes"), which is **not** a duplicate of this fix: it
targets a different defect class (ReDoS/timing) in the *same file*'s
`func_detail_regex`,

title: [Bugfix][GLM] Invalidate merged KDA convolution weights after refit
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087.

GLM-5.3 KDA lazily merges the q/k/v convolution weights into a single cached tensor for the fused causal-conv path. During online RL or refit workflows, the underlying q/k/v convolution weights can be updated after warmup, but the derived merged tensor may remain stale. Subsequent inference can then continue using old or dummy weights even after the model weights have been refreshed.

This change:

- adds explicit invalidation for the merged KDA convolution-weight cache
- invalidates the KDA cache before GLM-5.3 model weight loading
- covers both the direct model-loading path and the top-level CausalLM loading path
- keeps the merged-weight cache for normal inference when weights are unchanged
- retains version/storage checks as additional protection against direct tensor mutations
- preserves the hot-path behavior by rebuilding only when needed

This PR is a follow-up to #53906, which introduced the GLM-5.3 implementation.

## Root cause

The KDA layer builds a single merged q|k|v convolution weight tensor and caches it in `_merged_conv_weight`. That cache was not always invalidated when the source q/k/v conv weights were replaced. In online-RL refit/update flows, this allowed stale merged weights to persist across reloads and be reused in later inference steps.

## Fix

- add a version-aware merged-weight cache key in the KDA layer
- rebuild the merged tensor when any source conv weight changes
- add explicit invalidation hooks for the merged KDA cache
- invoke cache invalidation before GLM-5.3 weight loading so the next access rebuilds from fresh weights

## Test Plan

Run the focused regression test on a CUDA-enabled environment:

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda.py -v
```

Run the relevant GLM-5.3 model tests:

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next -v
```

Run static validation:

```bash
python -m py_compile \
  vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py \
  vllm/models/glm5next/nvidi

title: [Attention] Add B12X sparse MLA and DSA backends
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

This PR extends the optional B12X attention backend on NVIDIA SM120 and SM121
GPUs with non-compressed sparse MLA and its DSA indexer. The existing `B12X`
selector chooses dense paged attention or sparse MLA from the model's attention
contract; users do not select separate B12X attention implementations.

The integration:

- Adds B12X sparse-MLA and paged-DSA backend implementations using B12X's
  `Caps -> plan -> bind -> run` APIs and caller-owned workspaces.
- Routes DeepSeek-V3.2-family sparse attention through the NVIDIA model hook,
  which also covers compatible GLM-5.2 and non-Flash GLM-5.3 configurations.
- Emits physical KV-cache slots directly from the DSA indexer.
- Supports decode context parallelism with rank-local selection and the existing
  LSE-based attention reduction, without adding global candidate reranking or
  model-specific DCP optimizations.
- Fuses BF16 absorbed query projection and RoPE assembly directly into the B12X
  query workspace when the selected attention implementation advertises that
  capability.
- Plans against the finalized KV-cache page geometry and warms the decode,
  extend, and indexer signatures needed by CUDA graph execution.

This does not duplicate #54929. That PR adds a portable Triton fallback behind
`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`; this PR integrates the separately packaged B12X sparse-MLA
and DSA implementations behind the existing optional `B12X` backend.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used while developing this PR. I reviewed
every changed line and am responsible for understanding and defending the
integration end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Return closed Ling3 reasoning as reasoning in non-streaming
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Non-streaming `ling3` returns a closed reasoning block as `content` when nothing follows `</think>`. For the output `<think>reason</think>` the response has `reasoning=None` and `content="reason"`. Streaming `ling3` and the `glm47` parent return `reasoning="reason"` and `content=None` for the same output. The chain of thought leaks into the answer field.

`Ling3Parser.extract_reasoning` in `vllm/parser/ling3.py` demotes reasoning to content so that an unclosed `<think>` block (thinking budget or truncation) is reported as content. The demotion used `not content` as its trigger. That is also true for a fully closed block with no answer after it. The fix triggers on the absence of the closing marker instead. The existing `<tool_call>` guard is unchanged.

Expected semantics come from the parent's own test, `COMPLETE_REASONING` in `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`.

Not a duplicate. No open PR or issue touches this condition. #55485 edits the import block of `tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py`. The new test sits below that, so the rebase for whichever lands second is trivial.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py -q
pytest tests/parser/engine -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/parser/ling3.py tests/parser/engine/test_ling3.py
```

Reproducer without a model:

```python
from tests.parser.engine.replay_harness import MockTokenizer, _test_request
from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager

vocab = {"<think>": 1, "</think>": 2, "<tool_call>": 3, "</tool_call>": 4,
         "<arg_key>": 5, "</arg_key>": 6, "<arg_value>": 7, "</arg_value>": 8}
parser = ReasoningParserManager.get_reasoning_parser("ling3")(
    MockTokenizer(vocab=vocab, tokens=[]))
print(parser.extract_reasoning("<think>reason</think>", _test_request()))
```

## Test Result

Before: `(None, 'reason')`. After: `('reason', None)`.

New test with the fix reverted: `1 failed, 6 passed`. With the fix: `7 passed`.

## Purpose

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.process_weights_after_loading` detects when a
checkpoint's per-expert gate (w1) and up (w3) NVFP4 global scales differ,
warns once, and then dequantizes the whole fused `w13` with the gate's
scale anyway:

```python

    layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0], layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 1]
):
    logger.warning_once(
        "w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected."
    )
w13_weight_scale_2 = layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0].contiguous()
```

Filed as #54974, with a measurement on a real checkpoint
(`dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4`): 69.1% of gate/up pairs
mismatched, ratio up to 10x, all 43 MoE layers affected. Per
jahnclawdmonet's analysis in that issue, this multiplies the up half's
contribution to the expert's output by `gs_gate / gs_up`, above or below 1.

Apply the same policy vLLM already uses for the analogous FP8 problem

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Decode hot-path cleanups: strided KDA recurrent inputs, NoPE MQA query without concat, no duplicate router GEMM
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

One of three independent GLM-5.3-Flash perf PRs 

Three small, independent decode hot-path cleanups found while profiling GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, FP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`):

1. **KDA decode: read token-strided q/k/v/beta in `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`.** The decode path hands the recurrent kernel column slices of the merged `q|k|v` conv output and of the fused `qkvbfg_a` projection (beta); `fused_recurrent_kda` made each contiguous, i.e. 4 copy kernels per KDA layer per step (34 layers; ~11 us/layer at 64 requests, ~0.4 ms/step). The Triton kernel now takes explicit token strides; contiguous callers are unchanged. The stride check is pure integer arithmetic (no views) because the KDA forward is a CUDA-graph break and runs eagerly.
2. **MLA: write the absorbed MQA query token-major and skip the empty RoPE concat.** Without head padding the W_UK bmm now writes into a `(B, N, L)` buffer through a transposed `out` view (verified: one GEMM kernel, no copy, identical result). For NoPE models (`qk_rope_head_dim == 0`) the FlashInfer sparse backend then uses `ql_nope` directly instead of `torch.cat` with a zero-width `q_pe`, which took the slow `CatArrayBatchedCopy` path (13.7 us/layer at 256 decode tokens, ~0.75 ms/layer per 16k-token prefill chunk).
3. **Glm5NextMoE: do not compute the router logits twice.** `MoERunner` holds the gate (passed via `FusedMoEFactory`) and recomputes the logits (`moe_runner.py:897`), so the gate GEMM in `Glm5NextMoE.forward` was wasted (two bf16->fp32 GEMMs + reductions per MoE layer). Follows `DeepseekV2MoE` and passes a placeholder.

title: [Security] Honor num_frames in Molmo2 default video sampling
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
The Molmo2 video loader's default sampling branch (`frame_sample_mode` unset) returned every source frame and ignored `VideoTargetMetadata.num_frames`. A client can select that CPU backend through request `media_io_kwargs` on an ordinary chat video request, so a small MP4 could expand into gigabytes of RGB even when `num_frames` was 1. This change uniformly samples at most `num_frames` when that cap is positive, and still returns all frames when the cap is unset (`num_frames <= 0`).

## Changes
- `vllm/multimodal/video.py`: honor a positive `num_frames` in `Molmo2VideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` when `frame_sample_mode` is omitted.
- `tests/multimodal/test_video.py`: unit and loader tests for capped, uniform, and unlimited default sampling.
- `tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py`: `VideoMediaIO` path with `video_backend=molmo2` and `num_frames=1`.

## Codepath coverage
- Chat / messages / responses via `MediaConnector.fetch_video` / `fetch_video_async` → `VideoMediaIO.load_bytes` / `load_file` / non-jpeg `load_base64` → Molmo2 loader: yes.
- Direct `Molmo2VideoBackend.load_bytes` (same `compute_frames_index_to_sample`): yes.
- Decoder backends that call `loader_cls.compute_frames_index_to_sample` (OpenCV/TorchCodec/etc.): yes.
- `video/jpeg` comma-split path: N/A (does not use the Molmo2 sampler).
- GPU request-level backend stripping: N/A (`molmo2` is a CPU backend).

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open and merged PRs for `Molmo2VideoBackend`, `compute_frames_index_to_sample`, `frame_sample_mode`, and `video_backend` / `num_frames`. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51969 clamps request-level `num_frames` so clients cannot raise the engine ceiling; it does not make Molmo2's default branch read that ceiling. Other open video PRs cover GLM sampling, empty indices, or explicit frame-index selection. No open or merged PR closes this sink.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] GLM-4.7: stray arg tags must not leak into tool-call argument keys
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes a tool-call corruption in the GLM-4.7 parser: stray `arg_key` markup leaks into the parsed argument **key**, so the client rejects the call.

Observed in production against a GLM server run with `--tool-call-parser glm47`:

```
list_dir({"path</arg_key>": "/Users/user/Desktop/project"})
-> client error: "must have required property 'path'"
```

The client rejects the call, the agent loses the step, and the model retries with an invented path.

**Root cause.** `_glm47_arg_converter` matched the key with an unbounded non-greedy group:

```python
r"<arg_key>(?P<key>.*?)</arg_key>\s*<arg_value>(?P<value>.*?)</arg_value>"
```

`.*?` is non-greedy but it is *not* bounded by the delimiter it is scanning for. If the stream contains a repeated or stray `arg_key` tag, the engine backtracks past the first `</arg_key>` because that is what it takes to reach the following `<arg_value>`, and the extra markup ends up inside the key. On

```
<arg_key>path</arg_key></arg_key><arg_value>/tmp/x</arg_value>
```

the old code yields `{"path</arg_key>": "/tmp/x"}`, reproducing the observed string exactly. The mirrored `<arg_key><arg_key>path…` case yields `{"<arg_key>path": "/tmp/x"}`.

**Fix.** Match runs of non-`<` text so the key group cannot cross its own delimiter, and accept a run of closing tags so a duplicate is skipped rather than shifting the key:

```python
_ARG_KEY = r"<arg_key>(?P<key>[^<]*+(?:<(?!/?arg_key>)[^<]*+)*+)(?:</arg_key>\s*)+"
```

Both `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` are built from it, so the streaming path gets the same guarantee.

The unrolled possessive form is deliberate rather than the simpler tempered dot `(?:(?!</?arg_key>).)*`. `_compute_arg_delta` re-runs the converter over the whole accumulated buffer on every argument chunk, so the common streaming case is a *failing* match against a partial buffer — precisely where a tempered dot backtracks per character. title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Bound kpool prefill tail-seed stores by NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS
bodyExcerpt:
Prefill `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` stores into `tail[blk]` using `blk = tslot // kpool`. After prefix-cache churn, `tslot` can carry a **main-KV-magnitude physical id** while the tail tensor is a 1-block-per-request ring (`n_tail` << physical id). Decode already skipped `block >= n_tail`; seed did not.

## Measured (gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4)

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56037 **Crash D** (2026-09-07).

- Dying step: chunked prefill, computed=211200, scheduled=2338 (`2338 % 4 == 2` so the last chunk must seed the tail ring), `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={}`, `new_block_ids` around 3535–3578.
- `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3` on the dying image, GPU 0 only:

```
hipModuleGetFunction(..., _kpool_tail_seed_kernel)
ShaderName : _kpool_tail_seed_kernel
Memory Fault Error
Memory access fault by GPU node-2
```

Same probe with `if blk >= NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS: return` does not fault.

## This PR

Pass `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS = tail_kv_cache.shape[0]` into the prefill seed kernel (AMD + NVIDIA copies) and return before the store when `blk` is out of range.

**Out of scope:** mixed-length MTP decode (Crash C) and equal-length short MTP decode (Crash E) in #56037. Those are separate paths; do not close #56037 on this PR alone.

title: [RFC]: Per-KV-cache-group prefix-cache retention, with a hit-min exemption for hit-inert EAGLE sliding-window draft groups
bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

**Summary.** On hybrid models that carry an EAGLE-style sliding-window draft group (DFlash/DSpark-shaped drafters), that group hashes `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) + 1` block ids at *every* prefix-cache boundary and frees them *cached* onto the protected tail of the one LRU that all groups share, while — once it is exempted from the hit `min` — contributing nothing to the reconciled hit length. On a GLM-5.3-Flash deployment this one group spends 87% of the prefix cache and caps coexisting conversations at ~50K tokens each. A per-group retention interval, combined with exempting such hit-inert groups from the hit `min`, restored ~4× the coexisting-conversation capacity with the fine hit grid kept for the target model's groups, and a third party reproduced 99.95% cached across alternating 120K conversations. All numbers below are **deployment evidence from a vLLM fork**, not upstream verification; the code reading is against upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`. This RFC asks for agreement on the policy before any code is posted as a PR.

**Where the cost comes from (upstream `main` @ `22df3a3`, verified).**

- `--prefix-cache-retention-interval` (`vllm/config/cache.py:156-158`, `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:530`) reaches the coordinator as one scalar, `KVCacheCoordinator.retention_interval` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:158`), and is handed unchanged to every manager at both `cache_blocks` sites (`:306-326` base, `:740-768` hybrid).
- Everything below the coordinator is already per group: `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks(..., retention_interval=None)` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:432-436`), and each `reachable_block_mask` interprets it against its own block size and window (`:485-`, `:1010-`, `:1472-`).
- A sliding-window group needs `need = _contiguous_blocks_for_hit(window, block_size, use_eagle)` contiguous blocks at every retained boundary (`:898-908`, `:1028`); a full-attention group needs one block per boundary. Thos

GLM MTP constructs a `ParallelLMHead` during loading, then the proposer replaces it with the target model's head. This disposable vocabulary projection increases the loading peak before sharing takes effect.

title: [Bugfix] Detect NVFP4 in compressed-tensors mixed-precision checkpoints
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ModelConfig.is_nvfp4_quantized()` detects NVFP4 by looking for `"nvfp4"` in the quantization config's **top-level** `format` string. Compressed-tensors **mixed-precision** checkpoints declare per-group schemes instead — the top-level format is `"mixed-precision"` and never names nvfp4 even when groups plainly are.

Concrete case: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`format: "mixed-precision"`, `config_groups.group_1` = W4A4 float, `tensor_group`, `group_size 16`, per-group `format: "nvfp4-pack-quantized"`, targeting `mlp.(gate|up|down)_proj` — 56 of 64 MLP layers). The check returns False → `enable_act_fusion()` returns False → `pass_config.fuse_act_quant` stays False at **every** optimization level → `ActivationQuantFusionPass` never runs → the fused CUDA op `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` is unreachable (it is referenced only from that pass) and Inductor handles silu+mul+fp4-quant — which `enable_act_fusion`'s own docstring says it cannot: *"FP4 quant is always custom so Inductor cannot fuse it."*

Fix: when the top-level format is mixed, inspect `config_groups`. A group counts as NVFP4 if its per-group `format` names nvfp4, **or** it matches the NVFP4 scheme exactly (W4A4 float + `tensor_group` + `group_size 16` + symmetric), mirroring `CompressedTensorsConfig._is_nvfp4_format`. The strictness is load-bearing: **MXFP4 is also W4A4 float** (strategy `group`, group_size 32) — e.g. `INCModel3/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4-Mixed-CT-AutoRound` — and must not be misclassified. Non-dict (preset-name) groups are guarded; non-mixed formats never consult groups, so e.g. pure `mxfp4-pack-quantized` behavior is unchanged.

Design note, pre-flagged: a mixed-precision model is only *partly* NVFP4, so a model-level boolean is arguably the wrong shape for this question; if maintainers prefer keying off resolved per-layer schemes, I'm glad to rework — this PR is the minimal fix at the existing seam (single call site: `enable_act_fusion`).

title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Split leaked GLM think blocks out of content when extraction is disabled
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

With `--reasoning-parser glm45`/`glm47`, passing `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` (or `thinking: false`) disables the parser's reasoning extraction. For GLM-4.5/4.6 that is correct, because their templates honor the kwarg and the model emits no think block. GLM-5.3-family templates read neither kwarg, so the model thinks unconditionally, and the raw scratchpad plus a dangling `</think>` lands in `message.content`:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Simple question.</think>2 + 2 = **4**\n\n..."}
```

The fix is output-driven: when extraction was disabled but the output still carries a think block, split it with the thinking-armed engine config instead of passing it through. Tag-free output (a template that genuinely honored the switch) passes through byte-identically, so GLM-4.5/4.6 behavior is unchanged. The request-scoped engine keeps the unarmed config, so the streaming and id-space paths (`is_reasoning_end`, `extract_content_ids`) are untouched.

Scope boundary, stated plainly: the streaming path still cannot auto-detect this case, because by the time a dangling `</think>` arrives the scratchpad has already streamed. Auto-detection there would require buffering content for models that legitimately disabled thinking, which is worse than the leak. Operators hitting this should drop the ignored kwarg for GLM-5.3 deployments; the non-streaming leak this PR closes is the verified repro from the issue.

Relationship to existing work: #43728's alias work fixes models whose template reads one of the two kwarg names; it cannot cover GLM-5.3, which reads neither. #52410 is the same parser-template agreement class from the other direction.

## Test plan

`tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` gains three pins: kwarg-disabled with a dangling end tag (the leak shape, now split), kwarg-disabled with explicit tags, and kwarg-disabled tag-free pass-through (GLM-4.5/4.6 preserved). The tagged cases also assert the

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Take video placeholder timestamps from the pixel path's frame sampler
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55644.

GLM-5.3-Flash video prompts are expanded by one frame sampler and encoded by another.

- **Pixels**: `Glm5NextVideoProcessor.sample_frames` samples with the checkpoint's policy — `fps_interval = 2.0`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps)` — and `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it to get `grid_t`.
- **Placeholders**: `Glm4vProcessingInfo._construct_video_placeholder` emits one frame of placeholders per *timestamp*, and the timestamps come from `_get_video_second_idx_glm46v`, a second sampler on GLM-4.6V's constants — `DYNAMIC_FPS_THRES = {30: 3, 300: 1, 2400: 0.5}`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps * temporal_patch_size)`, then `[::2]`.

`Glm5NextProcessingInfo` moved the pixel half over to the checkpoint's own processor (`get_hf_processor`, `_get_vision_info`, `_get_image_max_pixels`, `_get_video_max_pixels`) but left the timestamp half on GLM-4.6V's. The two samplers agree only for source durations between 30 s and 300 s, where `target_fps = 1` makes `duration * 1 * 2` coincide with `duration * 2`. Outside that window the prompt gets a different number of placeholders than the vision tower produces rows, the counts first meet on the GPU in `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, and the resulting error inside a worker takes the engine core down with it — one malformed request kills the server:

title: [Bugfix][Core] Make encoder-decoder encoder-cache frees idempotent
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55733. The scheduler frees a request's encoder inputs on every step (`update_from_output` → `_free_encoder_inputs`), but for encoder-decoder models `EncoderDecoderCacheManager.get_cached_input_ids` returns all inputs each call and `free_encoder_input` unconditionally re-added `num_encoder_embeds` to `num_free_slots`. The budget inflates by the encoder size per decode step (100 → 300 in 5 steps in the repro), so `can_allocate` admits more concurrent encoder-decoder prefills than the cache allows. Track freed inputs per request; a re-allocated input (preemption/resume) is freeable again.

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

## Measurements

Serving image, calling the backend directly, 2-frame 1-second clip, `fps` and
`max_frames` set to the same value:

| requested | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 000 | 11.9 ms, +1 MiB | 3.1 ms, +0 MiB |
| 2 000 000 | 87.4 ms, +18 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |
| 20 000 000 | 857.5 ms, +156 MiB | 0.0 ms, +0 MiB |

Output is unchanged in every case: 2 indices for the 2-frame source, 900 for a
900-frame 30 fps clip, 2048 for a 10 000-frame one, and the default interval
still yields the same 60 indices as the bare sampler.

## Not a live exposure

Per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` do not reach the video loader today;
`chat_utils.py` still carries `TODO: Support per-request mm_processor_kwargs`.

## Purpose

Draft for applying and testing the complete local e2e enablement patch. This is
not a claim of merge readiness or full model correctness certification.

Enable the existing DFlash2 implementation to use
`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` as its target on NVIDIA GPUs, with
`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` as the seven-token drafter.

   and account for draft groups in shared-slot allocation and capacity checks.

No CUDA/C++ kernels, global speculative-cache defaults, or native MTP settings
are changed. The tested DFlash2 configuration explicitly sets

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend][Parser] Preserve text between GLM XML tool calls
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

  The Rust GLM XML tool parser entered a special post-call state after parsing
  the first `</tool_call>`. When ordinary text and another `<tool_call>` appeared
  in the same buffered chunk, the remaining buffer was consumed without
  producing the text or parsing the later call.

  For example:

  ```
  <tool_call>first...</tool_call>
  intermediate text
  <tool_call>second...</tool_call>
```

  The result depended on chunk boundaries: parsing the output in one chunk could
  return only the first call, while some streaming splits returned both calls.

  Return the GLM XML parser to text mode after every completed tool call.
  Intermediate and trailing text is now preserved, later tool calls are parsed
  normally, and equivalent input produces the same event sequence regardless of
  chunk boundaries. The behavior also matches the Python GLM parser.

## Test Plan

```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser glm47_preserves_text_between_tool_calls_across_chunk_boundaries

cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser  'tool::glm_xml::'

title: [CI] Reserve autotuning headroom for GLM TP2 PCP2 eval
bodyExcerpt:
# PCP autotuning OOM: mitigation candidate

Status: implemented and linted; **not GPU validated and not a merge-ready fix**.

The TP2/PCP2/EP GLM-5.2 NVFP4 case in [main build 87636](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87636#01a07f9c-18d7-4842-8ea3-de40c89c34c8) profiles successfully, allocates KV cache, then fails during FlashInfer autotuning. The stack is `compile_or_warm_up_model -> kernel_warmup -> flashinfer_autotune -> _run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs -> cutlass_fused_moe -> FusedMoeRunner::getWorkspaceInfo`. It requests 12.22 GiB on each B200 when only 7.67 GiB is free; the initial profiling reserved 33.46 GiB for KV cache at utilization 0.92.

The candidate adds `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` only to `GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP2-PCP2-EP.yaml`. On a 178.35 GiB device this reduces the requested engine budget by approximately 12.48 GiB, leaving more space for the later autotuning peak. This is a capacity mitigation, not a correction to runtime memory accounting. The estimate is not proof that all tuning tactics or evaluation batches fit.

Batch size 32768, context length 4096, concurrency 100, TP2/PCP2/EP, backend, fp8 KV cache, model, all 1319 questions, accuracy threshold and tolerance remain unchanged. The separate TP1/PCP4 synchronization failure still requires #55499.

## Existing work

Open draft [#49115](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49115) proposes moving autotuning before profiling. It has merge conflicts, failed pre-run checks and no reported GPU test result, so it must not be represented as a verified B200 fix. The CI budget mitigation is distinct from that production runtime change. Searches for PCP memory and the exact TP2-PCP2 config found no matching open budget mitigation. [#55671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55671) changes autotuning cache management and explicitly remains a no-op on pinned FlashInfer 0.6.18.

## Validation

- Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check`: passed.
- YAML parsing and shlex argument comp

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Saturate bf16->fp16 conversion in QuickReduce
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55345.

QuickReduce packs bf16 inputs into fp16 before the codec runs
(`quick_reduce_impl.cuh`, the `cast_bf2half` branch). bf16 covers the fp32
exponent range; fp16 stops at 65504. `__float22half2_rn` does not saturate, so
any activation above that becomes `inf` and propagates through the reduction,
poisoning the whole line — silently, with no warning and no numerical check.

The conversion sits *ahead* of the codec, so this affects every quantization
mode (INT4/INT6/INT8 **and** FP), not only the quantized ones.

## Test Plan

Two ranks on MI355X (gfx950), INT8 codec, one out-of-fp16-range value on rank 0
and 1.0 everywhere else:

```python
x = torch.full((n,), 1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
if rank == 0:
    x[0] = 1.0e30           # representable in bf16, not in fp16
out = qr.quick_all_reduce(x)
print(out[0].float().item(), torch.isfinite(out).all().item())
```

Same container image in both runs, only the built extension differs, so the
difference is attributable to this change and nothing else.

## Test Result

```
before: out[0] = inf     torch.isfinite(out).all() = False
after:  out[0] = 65536   torch.isfinite(out).all() = True
```

Other elements unchanged at 2.0 in both runs.

End-to-end on GLM-5.3 (TP4, MXFP4 + fp8 attention, 8192-token chunks) the clamp
is not measurable against run-to-run noise — the surrounding loop is
bandwidth-bound and the two `fminf`/`fmaxf` pairs ride along in registers.

## Scope

This is a mitigation, not a complete fix, and I would rather state the limit
than oversell it: with N ranks each contributing a clamped 65504, the fp16
accumulation can still saturate. What it removes is the case where a single
out-of-range value destroys the entire reduction. Keeping bf16 end to end for
bf16 inputs would be the complete answer, but that is a larger change with its
own cost, and worth deciding separately.

title: [BugFix] GLM-5: load msmodelslim-native checkpoints and drop MTP draft weights
bodyExcerpt:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Two problems loading official (msmodelslim-exported) GLM-5 W8A8 checkpoints into `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`:

1. **dotted submodule paths**: msmodelslim serializes the MHC and KDA gate modules as `attn_hc.fn` / `self_attn.forget_gate.A_log` while the model registers flattened names (`hc_attn_fn`, `self_attn.A_log`). Load now maps the ten dotted forms at load time via a `WeightsMapper`; already-flattened checkpoints are unaffected (the substrings never match).

2. **MTP draft weights**: the checkpoints ship the QuaRot MTP rotation (`rot.weight`) and the draft layer (`layers.<N>.*` for `N >= num_hidden_layers`). Those weights belong to the separate MTP model used with speculative decoding; without it they have no module to land in and the loader fails with `no module or parameter named 'rot'`. Drop them in the wrapper's `load_weights`, mirroring the reference Ascend implementation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — official GLM-5 W8A8 checkpoints (e.g. the msmodelslim-exported ones) load and serve instead of failing on the first weight.

### How was this patch tested?

End-to-end on Atlas 910B3 with the official GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 checkpoint (81 shards, 311 GB): loads cleanly, serves with the kpool backend, GSM8K-level gate 12/12; behavior verified identical to the flattened self-exported checkpoint (greedy outputs byte-identical incl. timing).

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool 32-page split (hybrid block_size=1152) GPU Memory access fault on MTP decode
bodyExcerpt:
ROCm gfx942, GLM-5.3-Flash, hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer: after the hybrid aligner lands on `cache_config.block_size = 1152`, the kpool indexer virtually splits 288-entry storage into **32-entry** paged-MQA pages. MTP decode then dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` (one `VllmWorker` abort → engine down). Not OOM.

Line numbers below are **vLLM `main` @ `156050598eea0bb1124b9c106b22ba4a8c56f82a`** (2026-09-04). Runtime numbers are from a gfx942 serving image derived from #53906 plus later local patches; they are labelled as such.

## Environment (runtime)

- 8× MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`
- Hybrid KDA + MLA + kpool indexer (`index_kpool = 4`)
- Serving image: #53906-era tree. Crash B already included the V2 slot-mapping `in_range` guard from #54296.

## Symptom

Two serving aborts on 2026-09-03, same family:

- Crash A (03:41Z): ~41054 computed tokens, first MTP decode after that prefill. Image did **not** yet have the #54296 V2 guard.
- Crash B (09:18Z): 5-way mixed batch (4 MTP decode + one 2304-token chunked prefill). `new_block_ids` around **3809–3813**. Prefix-cache hit ~93%, KV usage ~4.25%. Image **already had** the #54296 V2 guard.

Banner is `Memory access fault by GPU node-N` → that rank’s `VllmWorker` exits → engine down. Not OOM. An aiter GEMM-shape miss in the same logs is not sufficient (same shape had been served earlier without abort). `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens=[-1,-1]` is the async placeholder, not the address.

## Why 1152 becomes a 32-page split

`PAGED_MQA_PAGE_SIZES = (32, 64)` (`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:35`).

`Glm5NextIndexerCache.get_kv_cache_spec` (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py:145-152`; there is no `amd/attention.py` sibling) picks the virtual page as:

- native if `storage_block_size <= 64`
- 64 if `storage_block_size % 64 == 0`
- **else 32**

On this host the hybrid mamba aligner set `block_size = 1152`. With `index_kpool = 4`:

`1152 / 4 = 288`, `288 > 64`

title: [BugFix] Flatten tuple-valued layer caches in copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace
bodyExcerpt:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Hybrid models can bind one attention layer's KV cache as a **tuple of tensors** — one entry per cache role (e.g. an MLA latent cache plus auxiliary indexer/state pools). The prefix-cache block-copy loop in `copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace` called `cache.device` / `cache.data_ptr` on the tuple itself and crashed:

```
AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'device'
```

This flattens tuple/list entries before the per-tensor dedup and copy loop; non-tensor entries are skipped defensively. Plain tensor caches are unaffected.

Observed on a GLM-5-style hybrid (MLA + kpool indexer caches) where any prefix-cache hit aborted the worker on the first block copy.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — prefix caching no longer crashes for hybrid models whose layers bind tuple-valued caches.

### How was this patch tested?

- New UT: `tests/v1/worker/test_copy_kv_cache_blocks.py`
  - tuple-valued layer caches receive the block copies per tensor
  - plain tensor caches still work
  - empty copy list is a no-op
  - shared-storage views are deduped (no double-apply)
  - All 4 pass on Atlas 910B3 (NPU); teardown-only environment noise aside, the assertions all pass.
- End-to-end on a GLM-5 hybrid serving stack: prefix caching enabled + 8-way concurrency now runs the previously-crashing block-reuse scenario cleanly.

title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Register mixed page sizes in one cache group
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a startup crash of `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` on sparse-MLA (DSA) models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2). With the connector enabled, the engine dies in `register_kv_caches` before serving (GLM-5.2-FP8, TP=8):

```
RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 42072, 8448]' is invalid for input of size 130343768064
```

Root cause: registration reinterpreted the whole KV allocation with a single layer's block size,

```python
regions = raw[:tensors[0].size].view(-1, num_blocks, block_bytes)
```

which only divides evenly when every layer in the allocation has the same page size. DSA models break that assumption: a layer's MLA latent cache and its indexer key cache are both `MLAAttentionSpec` with the same block size, so they land in one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group whose page size is their sum, while the individual pages differ (576 vs 132 bytes/token, i.e. 36864 vs 8448 bytes at block size 64). With a layer-outermost layout the group's layers alias one allocation, and `num_layers * (mla_page + indexer_page)` is a multiple of neither page, so `view()` raises.

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is not a precondition. The indexer key cache is always `uint8` (128 fp8 keys plus one fp32 scale per 128 elements), so it does not scale with the KV cache dtype; at bf16 the pages become 73728 / 8448 and `gcd` is still 768.

Registration now derives each region from the placement metadata #51718 put on `KVCacheTensor` (`layers`/`layer_stride`/`block_stride`/`offset`) instead of reinterpreting the allocation with one layer's block size:

- a layer-outermost tensor splits into one `[num_blocks, block_bytes]` region per layer (per KV head group under LHBNC), using the tensor's own block stride;
- a block-outermost tensor stays a single region, as before;
- regions are deduplicated by address, so overlaid cache groups still register once.

This also fixes a latent misregistration in mixed groups where the division happens to succeed. Dedup was keyed on backing storage, so

title: [Bug]: DFlash2 spec-decode with a sliding-window drafter: admission (full_sequence_must_fit) and execution allocation both scale the drafter group's KV requirement with FULL sequence length -> admission deadlock above a block-size-dependent bound (~15.5K tokens at block-size 2304), engine crash on admission-clamp workarounds
bodyExcerpt:
## Environment

- vLLM v1, version `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (image `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-x86_64-cu130@sha256:2e771fa615452282cc331eb418b3ef21636fce355bea0491fca89e6d362ab703`)

- Model: GLM-5.3-class MoE + DFlash2 drafter (windowed drafter)

## Summary

With a sliding-window drafter, the spec-decode admission check sums per-KV-group requirements
`min(cdiv(N, group_block_size), cap)` against the UNIFIED free-block pool. The drafter's
SlidingWindowManager (block_size 16) contributes `cdiv(N,16)` — full-sequence-scaled, not window-scaled.
Above a pool-size-dependent bound (N ≥ ~15,537 at block-size 2304 with a 1,012-block pool), a single
request can never admit: it sits in WAITING for 600s (`Running: 0, Waiting: 1, KV 0.0%`) until the
request times out. The true sliding-window need is only `cdiv(2048,16)+2 = 130` blocks.

Clamping the ADMISSION requirement to the window need (130) removes the wedge but the engine then
crashes EXECUTION-side: `allocate_new_blocks` computes `num_required_blocks = cdiv(num_tokens, bs)`
RAW for the same manager — mid-prefill of 15,787 tokens it demanded 475 new blocks (held 513) vs
~459 free → `ValueError: Cannot get 475 free blocks from the pool` → engine death. The
`remove_skipped_blocks` mechanism IS wired and called per chunk with correct values (frees 383–406
blocks/call), but execution re-consumes blocks at full-sequence scale every chunk — held never drops.

title: [ROCm] Hold the router weight in fp32 when fp32 routing is requested
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55351.

`_get_moe_router_dtype()` returns `torch.float32` unconditionally for
`glm_moe_dsa`, and GLM-5.3's own config carries `"moe_router_dtype": "float32"`.
But `GateLinear` is constructed without `params_dtype`, so only the *output* is
fp32 — the weight stays in the model dtype (bf16).

`GateLinear` gates every fp32 router GEMM on `self.weight.dtype ==
torch.float32`, so those kernels are unreachable for DeepSeek-family models. That
includes the gfx950 kernel added in #54845, whose
`ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES` explicitly lists `(6144, 256)` — exactly
GLM-5.3's router shape. A log line at construction time:

```
gfx950=True, shape (6144, 256) supported=True, weight=torch.bfloat16
  -> fp32 path OFF
```

vLLM already has the mechanism for this. `force_fp32_compute` stores the weight
in fp32 *only* when the platform has no specialized kernel expecting the model
dtype, so it is a no-op wherever such a kernel exists. `nemotron_h.py` uses it;
the DeepSeek path did not.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GLM-5.3 (MXFP4 experts + fp8 attention),
`--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3. Same image, same flags, only this line
differing.

## Test Result

The path is reached:

```
gfx950=True, shape (6144, 256) supported=True, weight=torch.float32
  -> fp32 path ON
```

| | path off | path on |
|---|---|---|
| single stream (median of 4) | 171.3 tok/s | 175.6 |
| throughput, 64 concurrent | 2005 / 2219 tok/s | 1969 / 2198 |
| GSM8K (150) | 98.0 % | 98.7 % |
| GPU KV cache | — | 2,843,584 tokens |

I would rather be straight about this: **on my setup it is noise in both
directions**, and it costs ~230 MB per rank for the fp32 copies of the router
weights. So I am not claiming a speedup.

What the patch fixes is the inconsistency: a model that declares fp32 routing
gets an fp32 output from a bf16 weight, and the kernels written for that case
never run. Platforms where the specialized fp32 kernel is a larger win over the
generic fallback should benef

title: [Bug][ROCm] Sparse-MLA indexer reserves a 32 GiB decode-logits workspace during profiling (max_num_batched_tokens rows), costing 21 % of the KV cache
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On ROCm, the sparse-MLA indexer reserves the decode logits workspace at the theoretical upper bound during the memory profiling run, not at the bound the scheduler can actually produce. On a 1M-context model that single allocation is **32 GiB per GPU**, and since `WorkspaceManager.lock()` freezes the size after profiling, it is subtracted from the KV cache for the lifetime of the process.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, profiling early-exit branch of `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`:

```python
# Decode logits buffer, used by rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.
# batch_size * next_n <= hidden_states.shape[0] == max_num_batched_tokens
if _ON_GFX942 or _ON_GFX950:
    workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(
        ((hidden_states.shape[0], max_model_len), torch.float32),
    )
```

The comment states the bound correctly, but `max_num_batched_tokens` is a *prefill* bound. A decode step produces at most `max_num_seqs * (num_speculative_tokens + 1)` rows — for us 64 · 4 = 256, against the 8192 that get reserved.

## Evidence

Full GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`), TP4 on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, `max_model_len` 1048576, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, `max_num_seqs` 64, MTP k=3, fp8 KV, block size 16.

`torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(context="all", stacks="python")` around `profile_run()`, peak of the profiling run — one allocation dominates everything else:

```
peak 34.18 GiB
  32.00 GiB  n=1   largest 32768.0 MiB
    workspace.py _ensure_workspace_size <- workspace.py get_simultaneous
    <- rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer
   1.22 GiB  n=1   fused_moe.py _mxfp4_a4w4_stage2
   0.19 GiB  n=2   rmsnorm / fused_add_rms_norm
   … everything else is below 0.1 GiB
```

8192 · 1048576 · 4 B = 32 GiB exactly. It also explains a symptom that looks unrelated: the KV pool scales with `--max-num-batched-tokens` at 4.25 MB per batched token, which is one fp32 row over the full context. Measured on the same instance:

| `--max-num-batch

title: [Bugfix] Don't select the MHA prefill path for MLA impls that lack forward_mha
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`forward_mha` is optional on `MLAAttentionImpl` — sparse-MLA impls such as `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl` implement only `forward_mqa`. `MLAAttention._use_sparse_mha` did not account for that, so on **SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 5090)** any sparse-MLA (DSA) model — GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4 — dies with `EngineDeadError` as soon as a prompt is long enough to select an MHA prefill path.

⚠️ **Short prompts take the MQA path and succeed**, so a one-line smoke test passes and the server looks healthy. The failure only shows up under realistic prompt lengths, which makes it easy to miss during bring-up.

Fixes the two faults reported in #55757. They are sequential — resolve the first and you immediately hit the second.

### Fault 1 — `AttributeError` on `masked_mha_available`

`_use_sparse_mha` reads `self.impl.masked_mha_available`, but that attribute is only ever assigned by `SparseMLAImpl` (`sparse_mla_attention.py`). Any other impl raises:

```
AttributeError: 'FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl' object has no attribute 'masked_mha_available'
  -> RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ...
  -> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

Fixed by giving `MLAAttentionImpl` a `masked_mha_available: bool = False` class default, next to the existing `supports_pcp` default. Impls that support masked MHA keep assigning it themselves, so their behaviour is unchanged. This also lets the `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` on that line go away.

### Fault 2 — `NotImplementedError` from `forward_mha`

With fault 1 resolved, `prefill.use_dense_mha` can still select the MHA path, which calls `self.impl.forward_mha(...)` and lands on the base implementation:

```
File "vllm/v1/attention/backend.py", line 1106, in forward_mha
    raise NotImplementedError
```

Fixed by adding `MLAAttentionImpl.mha_available()`, which reports whether an impl overrides the default `forward_mha`, and returning early from `_use_sparse_mha` when it does not — so the selector cannot route

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.

title: [Bug]: `fuse_attn_quant` without `use_inductor_graph_partition` drops all piecewise cudagraphs on backends that cannot do FULL (-38 % on ROCm sparse MLA)
bodyExcerpt:
On an attention backend whose cudagraph support is below `FULL`, enabling
`fuse_attn_quant` **without** `use_inductor_graph_partition` removes every
piecewise cudagraph and does not get full ones in return. On GLM-5.3
(`glm_moe_dsa`, `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend`, gfx950, TP4, MTP k=4) it costs
**38 % throughput** and **+60 % TPOT**.

### The chain

`config/compilation.py:1257`:

```python
def set_splitting_ops_for_attn_fusion(self):
    assert self.pass_config.fuse_attn_quant
    if self.splitting_ops is None:
        self.splitting_ops = []
        if self.cudagraph_mode.has_piecewise_cudagraphs():
            logger.warning_once(
                "fuse_attn_quant is incompatible with piecewise cudagraph when "
                "use_inductor_graph_partition is off. In this case, splitting_ops "
                "will be set to empty list, and cudagraph_mode will be set to FULL."
            )
            self.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL
```

The backend then cannot honour `FULL`:

```
WARNING [compilation.py:1413] CUDAGraphMode.FULL is not supported with
ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend backend (support: AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH);
setting cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY
```

and the fallback picks the lossy branch:

```python
if self.splitting_ops_contain_attention():
    cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE   # would keep piecewise
else:
    cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY     # loses piecewise entirely
```

`set_splitting_ops_for_attn_fusion` has just set `splitting_ops = []` and even
asserts that no attention op is in it, so `splitting_ops_contain_attention()`
is **always** False here. The `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` branch is unreachable for
this path.

Resulting config: `'splitting_ops': []`, `'cudagraph_mode': FULL_DECODE_ONLY`,
`54 Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL)`, zero piecewise captures. With chunked
prefill most steps are mixed prefill+decode, so they get no cudagraph at all.

### Measured

Same replica, env switches byte-identical

title: [Bug]: `fuse_rope_kvcache` / `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` silently register zero patterns on MLA-only models, but their side effects are still paid
bodyExcerpt:
On an MLA-only model (GLM-5.3, `glm_moe_dsa`, ROCm/gfx950, TP4), enabling
`fuse_rope_kvcache` and `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` costs measurable
throughput while doing nothing at all, and nothing in the logs says so.

**Why nothing matches.** Both passes collect their layers with

```python
# rope_kvcache_fusion.py
attn_layers = get_layers_from_vllm_config(config, Attention)
# qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py — same line
```

`Attention` (`layers/attention/attention.py`) and `MLAAttention`
(`layers/attention/mla_attention.py`) are siblings — both
`(nn.Module, AttentionLayerBase)`, neither derives from the other — so on an
MLA-only model the dict is empty and no pattern is ever registered.
Independently, `fused_rope_kvcache_supported()` is implemented only in
non-MLA backends (`rocm_attn`, `triton_attn`, `triton_attn_diffkv`,
`rocm_aiter_fa`, `rocm_aiter_unified_attn`), so the inner condition could not
fire either.

**What is still paid, unconditionally:**

1. Two extra compile-range endpoints. `_set_compile_ranges` appends
   `rope_kvcache_fusion_max_token_num` (256) once per flag, so
   `compile_ranges_endpoints` goes from `[5461, 8192]` to
   `[256, 256, 5461, 8192]` — an extra graph specialisation.
2. `custom_ops: ['+rotary_embedding']` is force-appended
   (`config/compilation.py`), overriding Inductor's own rope lowering.
3. Two additional graph rewrites run regardless of matches
   (`pass_manager.py`):
   ```python
   if self.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache:
       self.passes += [SplitCoalescingPass(config)]
       self.passes += [ScatterSplitReplacementPass(config)]
       self.passes += [RopeKVCacheFusionPass(config)]
   ```

**Suggested fix (small).** `AttnQuantFusionPass` already does the right thing:

```python
if len(layers) == 0:
    logger.warning(
        "Attention + quant fusion is enabled, but no attention layers were "
        "found ... so no fusion patterns were registered."
    )
```

The two rope passes have no such warning. Emitting the same warn

bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
vLLM built from main (verified on 808f8cd3ac and 58ad1f3b89)
Serving GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, 2x H200 NVL (SM90), TP2, --kv-cache-dtype fp8,
--max-model-len 1048576, --max-num-seqs 32, MTP k=3.
The numbers below come from calling the backend directly inside that serving
image, so they do not depend on the serving flags.
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Glm5NextVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` forwards `fps` and
`max_frames` into `glm_sample_frame_indices` without an upper bound:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/58ad1f3b89/vllm/multimodal/video.py#L706-L726

The sampler walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and deduplicates only at the
end, so the intermediate list is sized by the requested value rather than by how
many frames the clip actually holds.

`GLMGAVideoBackend`, in the same file, gained `_MAX_FRAMES = 640` and
`_MAX_FPS = 30` for exactly this in #54935 (GHSA-58v5-2m8f-94pr). The glm5next
path did not get the same treatment.

**Measured**, calling the backend directly (no server involved), 2-frame
1-second clip:

| request values | result | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `fps=2`, default | 2 indices | 0.003 s |
| `fps=2_000_000`, `max_frames=2_000_000` | 2 indices | 0.088 s, +19 MiB RSS |

and on a 10 000-frame source:

| request values | returned |
|---|---|
| `max_frames=100_000` | 10 000 indices |
| documented default cap | 2 048 |

Both costs grow linearly with the requested number, so larger values scale to
multi-second walks and gigabytes of intermediate list, all for a clip that has a
handful of frames.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 KV cache rejected by SM90 sparse MLA plan(), and the indexer prefill workspace is sized in tokens
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

vLLM `main` at `98ed0856f` (right after #53906 landed), 2x H200 NVL (SM90), TP2,
CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18. Model: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4
(`LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`), `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on,
CPU offload connector with a 256 GiB region.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two independent bugs hit on the same deployment. Both are in code that came in with
#53906; both are still on `main`.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`.**

The fp8 KV cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as
`float8_e4m3fn`, but `FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder` hands `plan()` the storage dtype
(`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`, the `_SM90State(...)`
construction). The wrapper rejects it:

```
ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported
```

Startup dies there. Dropping `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` avoids it at the cost of 1.78x less
KV capacity (2,532,577 tokens instead of 4,503,445 on this hardware).

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in tokens, but its KV is pool-granular.**

`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py:303` takes
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size(vllm_config)` as-is. That helper returns a token count
(`max_model_len * 40` entries of 132 bytes), while this indexer's spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool` and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides by
`compress_ratio` at the same call site.

At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this reserves ~5.16 GiB per GPU
during the memory profile and locks it for the process lifetime, straight out of the KV
budget. Right-sizing it here moves available KV memory from 29.44 GiB to 32.06 GiB and
the KV pool from 4,503,445 to 4,904,494 tokens, with needle retrieval on 1M-token
prompts unchanged at 4/4. Originally reported by @nood-co1 in the

title: [Bug][ROCm] rope_kvcache / qk_norm_rope_kvcache fusions make GLM-5.3 8x slower on gfx950 (partitioning alone is fine)
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On ROCm (gfx950/MI355X) with GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`, MXFP4, TP4), enabling
`fuse_rope_kvcache` and `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` — which requires
`use_inductor_graph_partition` — makes the model **8× slower**. The fusions do
fire, and the outputs stay correct; it is purely a performance collapse.

## Measurements

8× MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP4, MTP k=4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`,
`--block-size 16`, prefix caching off, 128 concurrent requests, 16k-context
dataset. Three runs per arm, first (cold) run discarded.

| arm | throughput | TPOT | needle 92k |
|---|---|---|---|
| `use_inductor_graph_partition` only | **1973 / 1943 tok/s** | 10.79 / 10.55 ms | 5/5 |
| + both rope fusions | **278 / 231 tok/s** | **84.95 / 108.40 ms** | 5/5 |

The fusions are active — the startup line changes from

```
Enabled custom fusions: norm_quant, act_quant, allreduce_rms, mla_dual_rms_norm
```

to

```
Enabled custom fusions: norm_quant, act_quant, allreduce_rms,
                        rope_kvcache_cat_mla, mla_dual_rms_norm,
                        rope_kvcache, qk_norm_rope_kvcache
```

Accuracy is unaffected (needle-in-a-haystack 5/5 in both arms), and MTP
acceptance is unchanged (3.76–3.83). Only the step time explodes.

## Why this is worth reporting

`use_inductor_graph_partition` **on its own costs nothing** here — it runs at
full speed and is stable under load. So the partitioning is not the problem;
the two rope fusions it unlocks are.

This also cost us a misdiagnosis. On an earlier date the same configuration
made a production replica appear to hang: 64 requests with no progress for
seven minutes, one rank at 100 % GPU and three at 0 %. We treated it as a
deadlock and disabled the partitioning. It was not a deadlock — at 108 ms per
token instead of 10, a factor of 8 is indistinguishable from a hang from the
outside, and the rank imbalance follows from the fusion node.

title: [Spec Decode] GLM-5.3-Flash DFlash2 aux hidden-state capture
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable DFlash2 speculative decoding for GLM-5.3-Flash by implementing aux hidden-state capture on the target model. Related: #55423 (same goal, different aux-materialization path — see below; comment posted there with the structural analysis).

## Problem

#55423 materializes aux states as `hidden + residual`. GLM's mHC residual is a deferred-fusion structure: at each layer boundary the decoder holds a 4-tuple `(x, residual, post, comb)`, and the layer-k output is only completed by `MHCPostOp` (`mhc.py`), whose mixing weights live inside the `post/comb` tensors. A plain `hidden + residual` therefore captures an intermediate state, not the completed output of layer k that the draft was trained against. We believe this may explain the unisolated output divergence reported in #55423.

## Solution

Capture before layer k+1, materializing aux via `hc_post(x, residual, post, comb)` followed by `hc_contract` — structurally identical to the last-layer epilogue. KDA/non-mHC boundaries fall back to `hidden + residual`. Sequence-parallel gather skips the dense stages. The multimodal wrapper (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, the architecture of the official `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` checkpoint) declares `SupportsEagle3` and delegates to the inner text model, so the protocol unpack through `language_model.model` works natively.

Semantics adapted from SGLang `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` (#36507/#36708), Apache-2.0.

## Test plan

- [x] New suite `tests/models/glm5next/test_dflash2_aux_capture.py` (9 passed, 2 GPU-gated skipped): bit-exact vs independently materialized fp64 reference, KDA/residual-None fallback, adjacent-boundary enumeration, capture-on/off return shapes, next-layer tuple purity, wrapper `supports_eagle3` flag
- [x] Regression: `tests/models/test_registry.py` (379 passed), glm5next registry imports, `test_dflash_causality.py` (13 passed), mhc kernel + transformer-utils glm5next suites — all green
- [x] E2E on H200 (SM90) TP4: greedy DFlash2

title: [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups
bodyExcerpt:
# [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups

## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`) builds an `OffloadingGroupConfig` for **every** `kv_cache_group` and then asserts, for all of them:

```
assert group.tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0, (
    f"tokens_per_block={group.tokens_per_block} not divisible by "
    f"tokens_per_hash={tokens_per_hash}. "
    f"Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need "
    f"--enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes."
)
```

But `tokens_per_hash` comes from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which derives the hash granularity from **prefix-cacheable groups only** (`hashing_sizes = [... if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable]`). The two sides disagree about which groups are in scope, so any hybrid model with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (`CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable == False`) whose block size does not divide the cacheable groups' hash granularity crashes at boot the moment the OffloadingConnector is enabled:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Enabling prefix caching does not help — the message's advice cannot be followed, because the scratch group is excluded from hash-size resolution *by design* and its ring capacity is set by compression/lookahead geometry, not by the cache block size.

Where this bites: sparse-MLA hybrids that keep a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of pre-compression keys. We hit it deploying GLM-5.3-Flash (support proposed in #53906) on DGX Spark: per rank the layout is MLA + 4 GDN mamba groups at block size 3584 and an SWA drafter group at 64 (all prefix-cacheable, gcd → `tokens_per_hash = 64`), plus a kpool-tail scratch group at block size 4 → `4 % 64 != 0` → boot crash with any `--kv-transfer-config` offloading setup. bodyExcerpt:
# vLLM native Responses support for `additional_tools`

Investigation date: 2026-09-07

## Outcome

vLLM's native `POST /v1/responses` path does not handle persisted
`additional_tools` input items. A request with a typed `AdditionalTools` item
followed by another input item fails before inference with:

```text
AttributeError: 'AdditionalTools' object has no attribute 'get'
```

The fix needs to do more than ignore the item. `additional_tools` carries tool
definitions, and Codex's Responses Lite request shape can put the client tools
only in this input item while omitting top-level `tools`. Native vLLM support
therefore needs to:

1. consume `additional_tools` as request configuration rather than a chat
   message;
2. merge its tool definitions into the effective request tool list; and
3. omit the structural item when rendering conversation messages.

## Evidence

The OpenAI Responses schema defines `AdditionalTools` with `id`, `role`,
`tools`, and `type: "additional_tools"`. Its `tools` field is described as the
additional tool definitions made available at that item.

Codex's Responses Lite path uses this shape and may send no top-level `tools`.
That behavior is independently documented in openai/codex#31894.

The failure was reproduced against both the production and direct development
vLLM endpoints, ruling out the reverse proxy, HAProxy, load balancing, and
LMCache. The model never receives the prompt.

Observed production environment:

- vLLM: `0.26.1rc0+glm53.flash.nvfp4.luke.clean.r1.vllme75bcfd.b12x58a046f`
- deployed vLLM checkout: `3c2d5db8524f5831dfe3abf39f75c1abbf2a8161`
- `openai`: `3.3.1`
- `pydantic`: `2.13.4`
- Python: `3.12`

A source audit of upstream `main` at

title: [Bugfix][Sparse MLA] Lower the default indexer logits budget on integrated (unified-memory) GPUs
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55569.

On integrated (unified-memory) GPUs — `cudaDeviceProp.integrated == 1`, e.g. GB10 / DGX Spark — a long prefill through the sparse indexer exhausts memory and kills the engine. The indexer's prefill logits tensor is `(chunk queries × prefix pools)` fp32 per sparse layer and takes a **new size on every chunk** as the prefix grows. At the 512 MiB default of `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` a 200K+-token request streams hundreds of ~500 MB blocks of ever-new sizes through the caching allocator each step; on unified memory the allocator's segment requests exhaust the host and the driver fails (`NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`) before the allocator's OOM-retry can flush its cache. 64K–115K-token prompts are fine; ~231K reproduces it every time on GLM-5.3-Flash TP=2 across two Sparks.

## Change

Add `sparse_indexer_max_logits_bytes()` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py` and use it at every read of the budget (prefill chunk splitting, both DSA indexers' profiling-run reservations, the Qwen QSA indexer):

- `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` is honoured whenever it is set (unchanged behaviour);
- when it is **unset** and the current CUDA device reports `is_integrated`, the default is 64 MiB, which makes the indexer sub-chunk on the query dimension so the blocks stay small and reusable;
- otherwise the 512 MiB default is unchanged. No behaviour change on discrete GPUs.

## Test

2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13.0), `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2`, GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, `--max-model-len 262144`), one chat request with a 232,484-token prompt:

| | result |
|---|---|
| default budget (512 MiB), env unset, **without** this change | engine dead ~2.5 min into prefill; host `MemAvailable` drops ~6 GB in 40 s; `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`; without a host guard both hosts wedge (reproduced 4×) |
| `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=64` (env) | served; host memory flat (7.9–8.9 GB); arithmetic gate
