title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3] Expose auxiliary hidden states (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) from Glm5Next
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

DFlash / DFlash2 drafters for GLM-5.3-Flash (e.g. `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, `dflash_config.target_layer_ids = [5, 14, 24, 33, 42]`) consume the target's residual stream at a handful of layers, but `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` did not implement the EAGLE-3 auxiliary-hidden-state interface, so `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", ...}'` failed at init:

```
RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface but aux_hidden_state_outputs was requested
```

## Change

Implement `SupportsEagle3` / `EagleModelMixin` on `Glm5NextModel` and both model classes.

The value captured at index `i` is the stream **entering** layer `i` (HF `hidden_states[i]`), which is the convention the runner's `+1` mapping of DFlash's `target_layer_ids` expects. GLM-5.3's mHC layers defer the hyper-connection post-mix into the next layer's fused pre-op, so the plain stream is not materialized between layers: the capture applies the previous layer's post-mix (`hc_post`) and contracts the streams (`hc_contract`), exactly as the last layer does before the final norm. Non-mHC layers and the embedding already carry the summed stream. Sequence-parallel runs all-gather the captured value. No change when no aux layers are set.

## Test

2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2`, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, `--max-model-len 245760`, `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'`, together with the drafter KV dtype fix and the GLM-5.3 KV grouping fix (separate PRs, referenced below):

- init passes the interface check and the DFlash2 CUDA graphs capture
- arithmetic gate exact; per-request reasoning-effort levers unchanged
- single-stream decode 25.4 tok/s prose / 56.0 tok/s code (bare: 16.7; MTP ×3: 24.5 / 35.7); prefill 956 tok/s

title: [Core][GLM-5.3] Carry a GQA drafter's attention layers through the GLM-5.3-Flash KV cache layout
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash has a dedicated KV grouping/layout in `kv_cache_utils` (`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` / `_glm5_next_tensor_layout`) that aliases the MLA, kpool-indexer, tail and KDA state pages into one block layout. It admits only those spec types, so loading a GQA drafter (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) next to the target makes it return `None`; the generic page unification then fails on the indexer cache, which that layout deliberately does not unify:

```
NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.
```

## Change

Carry the drafter's attention layers through the GLM-5.3 path as one more group: its block is shrunk to the largest kernel-granular (multiple of 16) size whose page fits under the MLA page **and that divides the model's block** — with a sliding-window group present the KV cache coordinator only does block-aligned prefix-cache lookups, and a non-dividing block never lines up with a cached prefix (measured: 0% hit rate, every request re-prefilled) — and the page is padded to exactly the MLA page; the layout recognizer returns the group, and the three consumers (bytes per block, tensor allocation, max-memory accounting) size, allocate and count it. No change without a drafter.

The drafter's group is flagged `is_eagle_group` when the speculative config uses the EAGLE last-block drop. Left unflagged, the KV cache coordinator flags **every** group, which widens the Mamba groups' lookup window past what align-mode checkpointing produces and silently drops prefix-cache reuse to zero (`_warn_if_unannotated_eagle_mamba` describes this) — measured as a 0% hit rate on a repeated 37K-token prefix before this flag. Foreign attention layers are only treated as a drafter when a speculative config is set; the padded-page fit is applied on CUDA only (backends with a fixed set of kernel block sizes cann

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep the model dtype for regular attention layers under kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fp8_ds_mla` is the packed DeepSeek-MLA cache layout and only MLA layers can use it. When a GQA drafter (EAGLE-3 / DFlash) is loaded next to a DS-MLA target served with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, the drafter's plain `Attention` layers inherit that cache dtype and backend selection fails:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla, block_size=256, ...)
```

## Change

In `Attention.__init__`, keep the model dtype for regular attention layers when the requested cache dtype is `fp8_ds_mla` (the same effect as `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers`, applied automatically where the requested layout cannot apply), with a one-time log line. MLA layers are unaffected.

## Test

GLM-5.3-Flash (`fp8_ds_mla`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) + `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window GQA layers) on 2× DGX Spark, TP=2: the drafter's layers select FlashAttention with bf16 KV, the engine initializes, arithmetic gate exact, 25.4 / 56.0 tok/s prose / code single-stream decode with the drafter. Without this change the run fails at the selector as above.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3] Fit the kpool-widened sparse top-k buffer to the 2048-wide SM120 index without a config edit
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Let GLM-5.3-Flash serve through `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` with its stock checkpoint config, without the `index_topk=2044` hand edit that every SM120 / DGX Spark recipe currently applies.

`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` ships `index_topk=2048, index_kpool=4`. The kpool indexer widens the top-k buffer by the always-selected pool tail (`kpool - 1`) and pads it to a multiple of 128, so the buffer that reaches the sparse-MLA kernels is 2176 wide, while the SM120 sparse backend and its kernels are instantiated for an index width of exactly 2048. With #53969's effective-width check the stock config is rejected at startup (`requires an effective topk buffer width of 2048; got 2176`); without it, the kernel receives a 2176-wide page table.

## Change

- `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`: a shared helper `fit_sparse_index_topk(config)` — when `index_topk + tail` would overflow the 2048-wide index, use the effective `index_topk = 2048 - tail` (2045 for GLM-5.3-Flash; `select_k = index_topk // kpool = 511` pools, the same as the 2044 workaround) and log it once. The fitted value is written back to the config that was passed in, so the indexer and the attention backend agree.
- `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/mtp.py`: the MTP draft sizes its own `topk_indices_buffer` from the draft model config (a separate object), so it calls the same helper; without that the `glm5_next_mtp` speculative path still built the 2176-wide buffer and failed at init on the SM120 sparse-MLA backend (`no decode kernel for this shape: ... topk=2176`).
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`: the SM120 backend validation checks the fitted width instead of the raw config value.

No behaviour change for configs that already fit (DeepSeek-V3.2 style `index_topk=2048, kpool=1`, or hand-edited 2044/4).

## Test

2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13.0), `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2`, RadixArk/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 with the **unedited** `config.json`, `--kv-c

title: [BugFix] Mamba sparse retention keeps a state below each boundary under EAGLE/MTP
bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #53504

Prefix caching never hits on hybrid models running MTP/EAGLE spec decode. Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash in production: 0 hit tokens against 16,897 queried, silently.

The full-attention EAGLE lookup drops one block below what it matched, but latest-only Mamba retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, the default) keeps only the state at the boundary itself, one block above anything a lookup can ever request. The reconciled hit is always 0.

Fix: when the group runs under EAGLE, also retain the state one block below each reachable boundary. Costs at most one extra state page per request; non-speculative behavior unchanged.

Verified live on a 4x DGX Spark GLM-5.3-Flash deployment (MTP k=3, TP=4): an identical 8,901-token resend now hits 4,608 tokens, warm TTFT 2.66 s vs 5.88 s cold, warm output byte-identical at temperature 0. Regression test included (fails without the fix); `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` passes 92/92.

title: [Bugfix] Seed hybrid mamba state index with mamba_block_size on prefix-cache hits
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix an out-of-bounds read on prefix-cache hits for hybrid mamba models whose KV config contains a prefix-cacheable attention group with a block size smaller than `mamba_block_size` (e.g. a DFlash2/EAGLE sliding-window drafter group with block 64).

`MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot with `(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`. By then `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has reassigned `cache_config.block_size = min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`, so on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA + sparse MLA, mamba block 7168, drafter block 64/1024) the seed is in the wrong units. `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` takes it as `src_col` and `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`): cached prefixes of ≥ 8 mamba blocks fault (`Xid 31`, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync), shorter hits silently restore the wrong recurrent state.

The fix divides by `cache_config.mamba_block_size`, the unit used for mamba blocks everywhere else (`MambaSpec.block_size`, the preprocess kernel, the block-table width; `mamba_attn.py` already derives the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`).

Fixes #55600.

## Test Plan

No unit test is included; the failure needs a hybrid model whose KV groups include a smaller-block prefix-cacheable group. Manual verification on GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3, TP=1, DFlash2 `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `max_num_seqs=1`) on a DGX Spark, before/after on identical inputs.

## Test Result

- Prompt A = 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question: before → HTTP 500 in 0.2 s, `NVRM: Xid 31 ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`; after → completes in 11.7 s with 50 176 cached tokens.
- After: 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete; multi-needle recall on warm (cached) requests equals cold at 100k / 250k / 450k tokens (5/5 each); warm TTFT 8.7 s vs 139 s

title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba prefix-cache hit reads out of bounds: add_request seeds the state index with cache_config.block_size after it was lowered below mamba_block_size (Xid 31 / illegal memory access)
bodyExcerpt:
**Summary.** `MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot as
`(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`, but by the time it runs, `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has already reassigned `cache_config.block_size` to `min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`. For hybrid models that carry an extra attention group with a small block size (here: a DFlash2/EAGLE-style drafter group with sliding-window spec, block 64 or 1024), that minimum is far below `cache_config.mamba_block_size` (7168 here). The seed therefore indexes the mamba block table in the wrong units, and `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` → `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width without a bounds check. Above the row width this is an illegal memory access (Xid 31, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`); below it, the request silently restores the KDA/mamba state from an unrelated block.

**Where.**
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`, `add_request`: `(new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size` (main, ~L70-77).
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `_initialize_kv_caches`: `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size = min(participating ...)` (main, ~L298-305). The comment there already notes that a small-block group "would otherwise drag the global block_size below the real allocator block size and desync it from mamba"; the min still includes any prefix-cacheable attention group with a smaller block.
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` uses the seed as `src_col`; `_copy_mamba_state_block` loads `block_table_base + src_col` with no check against the row width. Mamba state blocks and the block-table row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`) are in units of `mamba_block_size`.

title: [Bug]: FlashInfer get_cudagraph_support() divides the *target* model's head count by the *draft* group's num_kv_heads, so spec-decode loses all CUDA graphs when the two models' head ratios differ (while the builder picks XQA and runs)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

vLLM `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (our serving image; the function below is unchanged on `main` @ `52358e6e19`, 6 Sep 2026 — line numbers in this report are `main`'s). 3x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, CUDA 13), tensor parallel 3, one node per rank, plus a 2-node TP=2 arrangement of the same image used as the control.

Target: GLM-5.3-Flash (EXL3 4-bit, out-of-tree quant plugin; the target's attention runs on a custom backend, `--attention-backend CUSTOM`, so the **only** FlashInfer KV-cache group in the engine is the drafter's). Draft: a DFlash drafter for GLM-5.3-Flash, `speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig(method='dflash', ..., num_spec_tokens=7)`, 5 layers, `sliding_window=2048`. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on both target and draft; fp8 draft KV is what selects FlashInfer for the draft group (with bf16 draft KV the selector picks `FLASH_ATTN`). `cudagraph_mode` left at its default (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), `compilation mode NONE`, `splitting_ops=[]`.

Our TP=3 arrangement pads head counts out of tree so that they divide by 3 (target 64 → 66 query heads, draft 32/8 → 36/9). That padding is ours, not vLLM's — but it only sets up the arithmetic below; the check itself is wrong for any target/draft pair whose head ratios differ.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`FlashInferMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support()` decides the CUDA-graph support level of a KV-cache group by dividing the **target model's** per-rank query-head count by **that group's** `num_kv_heads`. When the group belongs to the *draft* model, the two numbers come from different models, and the result is wrong. In our case it turns every CUDA graph in the engine off at TP=3 while the identical image captures them at TP=2 — and the runtime path that would actually run inside the graph (XQA decode) is selected and works.

author: NNNtrance

title: [Perf][Multimodal] Avoid scanning every source video frame
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`GLM46VVideoBackend` and `GLMGAVideoBackend` currently find each sampled frame
by iterating over every source frame until its timestamp reaches the next
sampling timestamp. This makes frame-index selection O(source frames), even
though both backends retain at most 640 frames. A long, high-FPS video can
therefore spend several milliseconds in a Python loop before sparse decoding
starts.

This change computes the first source-frame index at each sampling timestamp
directly. It corrects the computed index against the original floating-point
comparison at timestamp boundaries, so the selected indices remain unchanged.
It also stops after `extract_t + 1` samples when the caller will replace an
oversized result with uniform sampling. Dense, short videos keep the linear
scan because it is faster when most source frames are selected.

The online path is exercised whenever GLM-4.6V or GLM-GA receives video input:
the backend computes these indices before the decoder reads the selected
frames. The change affects only CPU frame-index selection and does not alter
video decoding, preprocessing, or model execution.

### Duplicate-work check

Open PRs were searched for `GLM video frame sampling performance`,
`source frame scan video`, and `GLMGA GLM46V video`. #54396 adds validation for
an unknown GLM-GA source FPS; it does not change the valid-FPS sampling loop.
Merged #46543 removed the full intermediate timestamp list from these loops,
but the loops still visit source frames one by one. This change addresses the
remaining O(source frames) scan and does not duplicate either PR.

## Test Plan

### Existing video tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/video.py
git diff --check
```

No test code is added. The existing suite covers GLM-4.6V dynamic FPS
thresholds, missing-duration estimation, even-frame padding, GLM-GA request
caps, short videos, and normal sampling.

title: [Bugfix] Pass CPU sequence lengths to TRT-LLM ragged prefill
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The B200 LM Eval PCP lane fails deterministically for both GLM-5.2 configs when the DeepSeek-v3.2 sparse-MLA prefill path calls FlashInfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`. Without trusted host sequence lengths, FlashInfer derives them from CUDA indptrs and evaluates `.any().item()`, which vLLM correctly rejects as a GPU-to-CPU synchronization.

This change:

- preserves the already-computed CPU query lengths in `MLACommonPrefillMetadata`;
- passes trusted CPU query/KV lengths to FlashInfer for new-token prefill;
- passes the corresponding host query/context lengths for context chunks.

This avoids the synchronization without disabling vLLM's sync guard or reverting PCP. It addresses the current synchronization failure in issue #49810; it does not claim to resolve every PCP issue tracked there.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR referencing #49810 and no open PR matching the TRT-LLM ragged/CPU-sequence-length fix. The older PR #49196 is a much broader PCP revert and is not equivalent.

AI assistance was used to investigate the failure, prepare the code and tests, and draft this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and confirmed running the relevant tests before PR submission.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \

title: [KV Cache] GLM-5.3-Flash: use the generic packed KV layout; CircularBufferSpec tail with speculative ring slots
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #53906 (GLM-5.3-Flash). Remove the model-specific KV cache grouping / tensor layout and the matching NIXL and Mooncake special cases by routing GLM through the generic packed (block-outermost) layout that DeepSeek-V4 and Qwen3.8-Next already use, and fix two issues in the kpool tail ring.

- `KpoolTailSpec` is dropped; the tail is a plain `CircularBufferSpec` (its manager already was `CircularBufferManager`).
- The ring is sized for speculative tokens, `kpool * cdiv(kpool + num_spec, kpool)` as the QSA ring does. With exactly `kpool` slots, a rejected pool-completing draft left the drafts behind it overwriting the committed keys the redo needs (covered by new CUDA kernel and index-level tests). The seed/decode tail kernels (NVIDIA and AMD) take the ring size and the tail view's strides.

title: [Bug]: KV cache offload crash-loops under NVIDIA Confidential Computing (TDX guest, H200 CC-On): cudaHostRegister is not allowed in CC mode (documented), and every built-in offload path depends on it
bodyExcerpt:
**Title:** KV cache offload fails under NVIDIA Confidential Computing: cudaHostRegister is not allowed in CC mode (documented), and every built-in offload path depends on it

## Summary

Under NVIDIA Confidential Computing (TDX guest, H200 CC-On, attested), all CPU KV-offload paths fail at engine startup because they ultimately rely on `cudaHostRegister`, which NVIDIA's Trusted Computing release notes (R580 TRD1, RN-12523-001, "Limitations in the SPT CC and PPCIe Modes") explicitly list as **not allowed in CC mode** (runtime: `cudaHostRegister`/`cudaHostUnregister`; driver: `cuMemHostRegister`/`cuMemHostUnregister`).

We measured `cudaHostRegister` returning `cudaErrorNotSupported` (801) for every size (64 MiB to 184 GiB) and every flag (default/mapped/portable/readonly). `cudaHostAlloc` works (rc=0, copies at ~4.9 GiB/s through the CC bounce-buffer path). Pageable `cudaMemcpyAsync` works. A failed registration is non-sticky (subsequent kernel launches succeed).

## Environment

- Phala TDX host, 2x Xeon 8558, 8x NVIDIA H200 (VFIO passthrough), guest 256 GiB
- vLLM 0.28.0 (tinfoil image), GLM-5.3 (~1T fp8, MTP-5, DSA)
- `--kv-offloading-size=180`, TP=8

## Failure chain (observed)

1. `kv_offloading_size` selects the native OffloadingConnector; `SharedOffloadRegion` builds `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_*.mmap` and calls `pin_mmap_region` -> `torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(...)` (kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py). Registration returns 801; the code warns and continues ("transfers will still work but may be slower").
2. After the offload pool is created, every serving engine generation dies at `warm_v1_block_table_kernels` with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not supported (cudaErrorNotSupported)`. Engine cores restart in a loop; the API never becomes healthy.
3. `simple_kv_offload` crashes earlier and harder: `cuda_mem_ops.py::pin_tensor` raises `RuntimeError` on the same rc=801.
4. With `--kv-offloading-size` removed, the identical config boots and serves.

On ROCm with AITER, startup dies during CUDA graph capture as soon as

RuntimeError: [AITER] /workspace/aiter_meta/csrc/opus_gemm/opus_gemm.cu:540

  Call aiter.opus_gemm_workspace_init() inside `with torch.cuda.stream(s):`

Traceback path: `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` →
`capture_model` → `cudagraph_utils.py:397 capture` → forward → AITER GEMM.

#### Root cause

AITER keeps the split-K partial-sum workspace in a registry **keyed by
`hipStream_t`** (`opus_gemm.cu`, `SplitkWsRegistry`). Eagerly it lazily creates

> cudagraphs, warm it via `aiter.opus_gemm_workspace_init()` on the capture
> stream.**

vLLM never calls it. Below ~64 sequences no captured shape resolves to a split-K
tuned entry, so the path is simply never exercised and the omission is invisible.

**This is not caused by user-supplied tuning tables.** I first suspected my own

title: [Bug]: --numa-bind is a silent no-op on ROCm images (numactl not installed)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
Image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly (also reproduced on a ROCm 7.2.3 derivative)
GPU: 8x MI355X (gfx950), TP4
Model: GLM-5.3 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM), MXFP4 experts + FP8 attention
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`--numa-bind` (added in #43270) is silently a no-op on the ROCm images, because
**`numactl` is not installed in them**, while `vllm/utils/numa_utils.py` shells out
to it.

`_probe_numactl_args()` catches `OSError` and returns `False`, so
`_resolve_numactl_args()` walks all three candidates (full args, CPU-only, `""`)
and returns `""`. The `logger.warning` in that function only fires when a
*different* candidate succeeds — when **every** candidate fails there is no
warning at all, not even at DEBUG level. The user passes `--numa-bind`, sees
nothing in the log, and gets no binding.

#### Minimal reproduction

```console
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly -c '
python3 - <<PY
import logging, shutil
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)
from vllm.utils.numa_utils import _resolve_numactl_args, _probe_numactl_args
print("numactl on PATH:", shutil.which("numactl"))
print("_probe_numactl_args(...):", _probe_numactl_args("--cpunodebind=0 --membind=0"))
print("_resolve_numactl_args(...) ->", repr(_resolve_numactl_args("--cpunodebind=0 --membind=0")))
PY'
numactl on PATH: None
_probe_numactl_args(...): False
_resolve_numactl_args(...) -> ''
```

No log output between those lines.

#### Why this matters

Per-worker CPU binding is not cosmetic on multi-socket hosts. Docker's
`--cpuset-cpus` binds the *container*; all five processes (EngineCore + 4 TP
workers) then share the same core set and the scheduler moves them freely — we
caught one worker running on an SMT sibling.

title: [Bug][ROCm] Sparse indexer clears the full max_model_len logits buffer every decode step: 17% throughput on a 1M context
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

ROCm 7.2.3, MI355X (gfx950), TP4, vLLM main.
GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`, hidden 6144, 256 experts), `--max-model-len 1048576`,
MTP k=3, 64 concurrent requests.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On ROCm, the DeepSeek-V3.2 style sparse indexer clears its entire logits buffer
on every decode step, even though the consumer only ever reads up to the real
sequence lengths. The buffer is sized `(B * next_n, max_model_len)`, so with a
1M context window this is a large amount of pure overhead.

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`, both ROCm paths:

```python
# HIP indexer kernel path
out_logits.fill_(float("-inf"))
...
# deepgemm path
out_logits.nan_to_num_(float("-inf"))
```

Profiled with the torch profiler, 20 decode iterations:

| load | kernel | share of GPU time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 request | `__amd_rocclr_fillBufferAligned` | **4.5 %** |
| 64 concurrent | `nan_to_num` (vectorized_elementwise) | **6.4 %** |

Sizing: at 64 requests with MTP k=3 the buffer is `256 x 1048576 x 4 B = 1.07 GB`,
while an 8000-token context uses 8.2 MB of it — **0.76 %**. The arithmetic matches
the measurement: 1.07 GB written at ~4 TB/s is 268 µs, and the profiler shows
239.6 µs per call.

### Why it looks unnecessary

The same caller (`sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py`) passes **`clean_logits=False`**
on the CUDA path and does not clear at all. That works because the consumer,
`torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode(logits, next_n, seq_lens, ...)`, is given the
real per-request sequence lengths and never reads past them. The region beyond
`seq_lens` is dead on every platform.

ROCm has no equivalent to `clean_logits` and clears unconditionally.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Keep the AITER allreduce compile range within AITER's runtime cutoff
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55344.

`vllm/config/vllm.py` derives the compile range of the fused allreduce+RMSNorm
pass from `AiterCustomAllreduce.effective_max_size()`, which only looks at
`MAX_SIZE`. AITER's runtime eligibility check is `min(_car_max_size, max_size /
2)`, where `_car_max_size` comes from `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE` and defaults to
a fixed 64 MiB that does not grow with the registered pool.

When the two disagree, the pass is compiled for message sizes AITER rejects.
`custom_fused_ar_rms()` then returns `None`, and
`_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` asserts on it — the server fails to
start with a bare `AssertionError` instead of falling back to RCCL. An env var
meant to *narrow* custom-AR usage should not prevent startup.

This makes `effective_max_size()` return what AITER will actually accept, so the
pass is never compiled for sizes that get rejected.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), TP4, GLM-5.3 (`hidden_size=6144`, bf16),
`--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, AITER custom AR and `fuse_allreduce_rms`
enabled. Same image, same model, same flags in both runs — only the env var and
this patch differ:

```
AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE=1048576 vllm serve <model> -tp 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
```

## Test Result

Before (unmodified tree):

```
compile_ranges_endpoints: [5461, 8192]
ERROR _aiter_ops.py:956 in _rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl
      assert result is not None
AssertionError
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
-> died after 160 s
```

After:

```
compile_ranges_endpoints: [85, 8192]      # 1 MiB / (6144 * 2) = 85 tokens
-> serving after 340 s, zero AssertionErrors
GSM8K 49/50 = 98.0 %
```

The range now matches the cutoff exactly, which is the intended behavior: with a
1 MiB cutoff the fusion is simply out of scope for realistic batch sizes, and
those fall back to RCCL as they should.

No change with the default (`AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE` unset): `min(MAX_SIZE //
2, 64 MiB)` is `min(64 MiB, 64 MiB)`, i.e. the previous valu

title: [Bug][ROCm] gfx950 FP32 router GEMM is unreachable for DeepSeek-family models: shape (6144, 256) is listed but the weight is bf16
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

ROCm 7.2.3, MI355X (gfx950), TP4, vLLM main + #54845.
Model: GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`, `hidden_size=6144`, `n_routed_experts=256`, bf16).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The gfx950 low-M FP32 router GEMM added in #54845 never runs for DeepSeek-family
models, including the `(6144, 256)` shape it explicitly supports.

`GateLinear` gates the path on `self.weight.dtype == torch.float32`, but
`deepseek_v2.py` constructs it without `params_dtype`, so the weight stays in the
model dtype (bf16):

```python
self.router_dtype = _get_moe_router_dtype(config)
self.gate = GateLinear(
    config.hidden_size,
    config.n_routed_experts,
    out_dtype=self.router_dtype,     # fp32 output ...
    prefix=f"{prefix}.gate",         # ... but the weight stays bf16
)
```

This is inconsistent with what the same function asks for:
`_get_moe_router_dtype` returns `torch.float32` unconditionally for
`model_type == "glm_moe_dsa"`, and GLM-5.3's own config carries
`"moe_router_dtype": "float32"`. The routing is declared fp32; the weight is not.

A log line at construction time makes it visible:

```
NACHWEIS Router-GEMM: gfx950=True, shape (6144, 256) supported=True,
                      weight=torch.bfloat16, bias=False -> fp32 path OFF
```

So `(6144, 256)` is in `ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES` and the hardware
matches, but the path is never taken. The same applies to every DeepSeek-family
model going through `deepseek_v2.py`.

title: [ROCm] gfx950 top-k policy is gated on topK==1024, leaving index_topk=2048 models (GLM-5.x) on the generic 10-way split
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The measured gfx950 policy for the sparse-attention indexer's top-k, added in #52882, is gated on `topK == 1024`. Models with `index_topk: 2048` — GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 — never reach it and fall back to the generic `multipleBlocksPerRowConfig = 10` with 512 threads per split block.

On MI355X that is the wrong choice for **every shape we measured**. A policy calibrated for `topK == 2048` gives a median 25 % and up to 64 % reduction in kernel time, with no shape getting slower and identical results.

## Where

`csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`, `top_k_per_row_decode`:

```cpp
const bool useGfx950DeviceLengthAwareTopK1024 =
    topK == 1024 && numRows > 64 && numRows <= 256 && gfx950;   // ~line 754
const bool useGfx950TopK1024 =
    topK == 1024 && numRows <= 64 && gfx950;                    // ~line 793
int multipleBlocksPerRowConfig = 10;                            // everything else
```

## Why the gap is larger, not smaller, at topK=2048

The merge kernel walks `B * topK` candidates in a **single** block per row:

```cpp
vllm::topKPerRowDecode<1024, true, false, true>
    <<<numRows, 1024, ...>>>( ..., multipleBlocksPerRowConfig * topK, ... );
```

At topK=1024 with B=10 that is 10 240 candidates; at topK=2048 it is **20 480**. The cost #52882 set out to remove is twice as large for the models that do not get the fix.

rocprofv3, 4 rows / 2 000 active columns, MI355X, GLM-5.3 (`index_topk: 2048`):

| kernel | grid | median |
|---|---|---|
| `topKPerRowDecode<1024,true,false,true>` (merge) | 4 × **1** | **95.4 µs** |
| `topKPerRowDecode<512,true,true,false>` (split) | 4 × 10 | 5.0 µs |

The split is irrelevant; the merge is the entire cost. In a full decode profile this kernel held 12 % of GPU time.

## Short contexts are the worst case, not long ones

`numColumns` is `logits.size(1)`, and the indexer's logits are allocated at `max_model_len` (`fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(..., max_model_len=max_model_len)`). With a 1M model length the two-stage path is therefo

title: [Security] Cap GLMGA video sampling to prevent request-driven resource exhaustion
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- Add hard class-level upper bounds (`_MAX_FRAMES=640`, `_MAX_FPS=30`) to `GLMGAVideoBackend` so that request-controlled `fps` and `max_frames` values via `media_io_kwargs` cannot create disproportionately large intermediate list allocations.
- Clamp `extract_t` to `total_frames_num`, ensuring the index list never exceeds the actual frame count of the video, regardless of sampling parameters.
- Add regression tests verifying extreme values are bounded and normal operation is unchanged.

## Root Cause

`GLMGAVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` computes `extract_t = min(int(duration * target_fps), max_frames)` where both `target_fps` and `max_frames` are controllable via request-level `media_io_kwargs`. When `total_frames_num < extract_t`, a list comprehension with `range(extract_t)` creates an attacker-sized intermediate allocation (e.g. 500k entries for a 2-frame video) that is subsequently deduplicated to just the actual frame count.

## Fix

Three layers of defense, following the pattern established by `GLM46VVideoBackend`:

1. **Cap `target_fps`** to `_MAX_FPS` (30) -- request values above this are clamped.
2. **Cap `max_frames`** to `_MAX_FRAMES` (640) -- request values above this are clamped.
3. **Clamp `extract_t` to `total_frames_num`** -- the critical invariant: there can never be more unique frame indices than there are frames in the video.

## Test Plan

- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_extreme_values_bounded_by_total_frames` -- 2-frame video with fps=500k, max_frames=500k produces at most 2 indices.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_class_cap_overrides_kwargs_max_frames` -- max_frames=100k from kwargs is clamped to 640.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_class_cap_overrides_target_fps` -- fps=500k is clamped to 30.
- [x] `TestGLMGASamplingCaps::test_normal_operation_unchanged` -- normal 1000-frame video with fps=2 produces expected results.
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass.

title: [Bugfix] Reject invalid GLM kpool indices
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3 kpool top-k can produce fewer valid entries than the allocated `select_k` width for short rows. The kernels do not promise to write the remaining slots, so allocating `pool_topk` with `torch.empty` can leave arbitrary positive values that are later treated as pool IDs and expanded into out-of-range sparse-attention token indices.

This change adds two defensive layers:

1. Initialize the prefill and decode pool-topk destinations with the `-1` sentinel.
2. Reject pool IDs outside the completed-pool count in the NVIDIA and AMD fused expansion kernels and in the current prefill fallback.

The regression covers valid pool IDs, negative sentinels, positive out-of-range IDs, and an incomplete tail. Only tokens from valid completed pools and the legitimate tail survive.

This was originally developed in https://github.com/ZJY0516/vllm/pull/8 while https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53906 was still pending. Now that #53906 is merged, this is the upstream-main version.

## Why this is not duplicating existing work

Before opening this PR, I searched open PRs for references to #53906, `GLM kpool invalid indices`, `pool_topk expand_pools`, and the broader `kpool` term. No open PR carries this exact sentinel initialization plus completed-pool bounds check.

The closest active changes are orthogonal: #54951 changes kpool row sharding but does not initialize unwritten top-k slots or validate expanded pool IDs, while #53969 concerns SM120 NoPE/effective-width behavior.

## Test plan and results

Commands run from an isolated Python 3.12 venv:

title: [Bug][DCP] GLM-5.3 dense prefill consumes uninitialized K rows on non-owner ranks
bodyExcerpt:
### Problem

Following the GLM-5.3 report in #50095, TP4/DCP4 generation with Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 is deterministically incoherent while matched TP4/DCP1 is coherent. This remains after applying the earlier #50005 correctness fix and after disabling the direct DCP communication paths, so it is a separate bug.
The GLM-5.3 problem is originally reported by @ehfd 

### Root cause

NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 dense prefill requests normalized/rotated K materialization from fused_norm_rope on every DCP rank. The fused kernel currently returns when slot_mapping is negative. Under DCP, a negative local slot can mean that another rank owns the cache row; it does not mean that the dense-prefill K row is unused. As a result, non-owner ranks leave kv_c_out and k_pe_out uninitialized, and dense prefill consumes those buffers.

Cache ownership and K materialization need separate guards: materialize the requested K outputs on every rank, but retain the negative-slot guard before owner-local cache writes.

### Validation

On 4x GB200 with greedy decoding, chunked prefill, prefix caching, FP8 KV cache, and CUDA graphs enabled, the narrow fix makes DCP4 token output exactly match DCP1 for:

- 512 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 222258a1...
- 1536 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 76643708...
- 1024 cached plus 1536 uncached prompt tokens: SHA256 4a150ea6...

The model run used the matching cu130 binary/source pair at 570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e with #50005 and the narrow fix overlaid. The same failing guard is unchanged on current main ee3c00bbf47e0ef7e975705cc980b06ee5576bb0; a current-main native build is still in progress and will be added to the PR validation.

A focused current-main regression test also passes and verifies that K outputs are materialized while MLA/indexer caches remain untouched on a non-owner rank.

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Materialize prefill keys on non-owner ranks
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #54907 and follows the GLM-5.3 report in #50095.

NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 dense prefill consumes normalized/rotated K outputs on every DCP rank. The fused kernel treated a negative local cache slot as an unconditional early return, but under DCP it often means that another rank owns the cache row. Non-owner ranks therefore left `kv_c_out` and `k_pe_out` uninitialized.

This patch separates materialization from cache ownership: pid 1 produces requested K outputs even without a local slot, then returns before MLA/indexer cache writes. Owner-sharded cache storage is unchanged.

This is not duplicate work. #50005 fixed query and DCP combine routing; the GLM-5.3 failure reproduces after that patch. Duplicate searches found no open PR for #50095 or this materialization defect.

title: [Bug]: KDA/gated-delta-rule chunked-scan buffers are outside memory profiling — runtime OOM at large --max-num-batched-tokens
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

The chunked-scan buffers in the gated-delta-rule (KDA) path scale linearly with
`--max-num-batched-tokens`, are allocated transiently inside the forward pass, and are **not
covered by vLLM's startup memory profiling**. The KV cache is therefore sized as if that memory
were free, and above a certain chunk size the engine dies at runtime — mid-request, after having
served traffic.

### Observed

GLM-5.3-Flash (45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention + 11 sparse MLA), 1× MI350X (gfx950),
ROCm 7.2.3, TP1, MXFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.
16 concurrent requests of ~38k tokens each.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | successful | failed | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 192 … 65 536 | 16 / 16 | 0 | stable across 3 runs each |
| **81 920** | **5 / 16** | **11** | engine shut down |
| **131 072** | **4 / 16** | 12 | engine shut down |

```
(Worker) ERROR  File ".../flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk_delta_h.py", line 357,
                  in chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
(Worker) ERROR    v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None
(Worker) ERROR  torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB.
                  GPU 0 has a total capacity of 287.98 GiB of which 0 [bytes is free]
(APIServer) INFO [shutdown] EngineCore process manager: using 15.0s ROCm cleanup grace
                  after immediate request abort
```

Startup reported no problem — `GPU KV cache size: 6,940,947 tokens` at 81,920, and the memory
profiling line looked healthy.

### Mechanism

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` allocates two buffers proportional to the token count in the batch:

```python
B, T, Hg, K, V = *k.shape, u.shape[-1]
H  = u.shape[-2]
BT = chunk_size                      # FLA_CHUNK_SIZE = 64, hard-coded in ops/utils.py:31
...
N, NT = len(cu_seqlens) - 1, len(chunk_indices)
h     = k.new_empty(B, NT, H, V, K)          # NT = ceil(T / 64)  -> linear in T
v_new = torch.empty_like(u) if save_new_value else None

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Disable custom allreduce when expandable_segments is enabled
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Refs #42609, ROCm/aiter#4174.

With `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, custom allreduce's CUDA-graph buffer registration fails at `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` / `hipIpcGetMemHandle` with `invalid argument` — VMM-backed allocations cannot be exported via IPC — which kills every TP worker during engine startup (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh` `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta`).

This broke the AMD CI LoRA TP shards, which set `expandable_segments` to avoid OOM (builds 87038/87059, `test_llama_lora_tp4_fully_sharded_loras` / `test_chatglm3_lora_tp4_fully_sharded_loras`). #55094 repaired those CI jobs config-side by dropping the env var, but the same crash still hits any deployment that combines expandable segments with TP > 1 (#42609).

Change: `CustomAllreduce.__init__` now detects `expandable_segments:True` in `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` / `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF` and disables custom allreduce with a warning, falling back to the other allreduce backends — turning a hard startup crash into a supported (slightly slower) configuration. The guard runs before any IPC buffer allocation, so it costs nothing.

Relationship to #55094: complementary, not duplicate. #55094 fixes the two CI jobs; this PR defuses the underlying landmine for all users. With both, the LoRA TP jobs pass either way.

## Test Plan

New `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_custom_allreduce_disabled_with_expandable_segments` (parametrized over both env vars), using the file's existing monkeypatch style; needs no GPU — the guard fires before any device access.

## Test Result

Verified locally: with the env var set, `CustomAllreduce(...)` returns with `disabled=True` and the warning; without it, the guard is not taken and init proceeds. The AMD LoRA TP jobs exercise the path end-to-end on CI.

## Duplicate-work check

#55094 (merged) is the CI-side fix for the same symptom; #42609 tracks the code-side issue this PR addresses. No other open PR found at the time of writing.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Wait for the previous PP tensor sends before the next forward pass
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes silent output corruption under pipeline parallelism introduced by #49274.

**Symptom.** GLM-5.3 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`) served with
`--pipeline-parallel-size 4` (4×H200) or `8` (8×H100), `--enable-chunked-prefill`
(`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`), `--enable-prefix-caching`, bf16 KV cache: prompts of roughly
8.2k–12k tokens come back as garbage on most fresh prefills (reasoning ends after 1–100 tokens,
then digit soup such as `1.0.0.0.5,0.9,0.1…` or `locklocklock…`). Longer prompts fail at a lower
rate. With a strict `json_schema` the grammar still holds, so the output is `{` followed by
legal whitespace up to `max_tokens`. Nothing is logged. Because the corrupted prefill is written
to the prefix cache, an affected prompt then fails deterministically on every repeat until its
blocks are evicted — which is how this was first reported to us as "one specific 31k-token prompt
always collapses, a one-character change to the system message fixes it".

**Bisection (the strongest evidence).** Same node, weights, flags and traffic throughout; each
build probed over a port-forward with a unique `cache_salt` per request so every trial is a fresh
prefill. "Garbage" = the probe above; "strict schema" = a `json_schema` whose only legal document
is a sentinel string, sent with a 9,357-token prompt.

| build | garbage at 8.3k–9.5k tokens | strict schema @ 9,357 tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.28.0` (PP) | 0/44 | n/a (older masking bug) |

title: [Kernel][Quantization] Cut transient memory in NVFP4 Marlin scale-factor computation
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor` in `marlin_utils_fp4.py` finds the largest NVFP4 weight scale by materializing an FP32 copy of the whole scale tensor, a boolean mask, and a gathered copy of the positive entries. The MoE paths (`prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin`, `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`) call it on the scales of **all experts at once**, so for a 288-expert model such as GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 one call touches about 300M elements and allocates several GiB of transient device memory during weight loading. On unified-memory machines with little headroom at load time (DGX Spark GB10, #50925) that spike can fail the load or push the driver into the memory-pressure spiral reported by the community.

This PR reduces the input tensor directly. The returned factor is unchanged:

- a max commutes with the exact multiplication by `2**7`;
- non-positive scales never win the max when a positive scale exists, and an all-non-positive tensor still returns `1.0`;
- an empty tensor returns `1.0` as before.

One deliberate behavior change: a NaN scale now raises `ValueError` instead of being silently excluded from the max. Happy to drop that if maintainers prefer the old silent behavior.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_marlin_scale_factor.py`: the previous implementation is kept verbatim as the oracle and compared against the new one for fp16/bf16 inputs, 1-D/2-D/3-D shapes, and inputs with zeros, negatives, all zeros, all negative, already-normalized values, and the `a_dtype=half` early return; plus range, empty-tensor, and NaN tests. A CUDA-only test asserts the call allocates no tensor-sized temporaries on a `(288, 512, 256)` bf16 input.
- `pre-commit` (ruff check / ruff format) on the two files.

```

```

CPU run (torch 2.13, the CUDA test skipped): `21 passed, 1 skipped`.

title: [Bugfix] Skip non-participating KV groups in offloading divisibility assert
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
Native KV offloading (`OffloadingConnector`) is unbootable on hybrid models that carry a **non-participating scratch group**, e.g. GLM5Next's `KpoolTail` — a 1-block/req circular buffer (`block_size=index_kpool=4`) that opts out of prefix caching by design. The divisibility assert in `build_offloading_config()` iterated every group:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=1152.
Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes()` already excludes non-participating groups from both the GCD and its own divisibility check — this patch mirrors that in `build_offloading_config()`.

## Changes
- `build_offloading_config()`: skip groups whose spec returns `participates_in_prefix_caching == False` in the divisibility assert; fall back to asserting on all groups if nothing participates.
- Regression tests (`tests/v1/offloading/test_build_offloading_config.py`):
  - a MLA (block 1152) + KpoolTail (block 4) group set that boots an offloading config (crashed on stock code),
  - divisibility is still enforced for participating groups,
  - the all-non-participating fallback path.

## Test plan
- [x] New unit tests added under `tests/v1/offloading/`
- [x] Verified on GLM-5.3-Flash (KDA+MLA hybrid with KpoolTail): engine boots with `--kv-offloading-size` where stock code crashed at init (3/3 attempts)

Follow-up: a second PR fixes three later crashes in the offloading scheduler that only surface once this lands and a KpoolTail group is actually scheduled.

title: [Bugfix] Guard KpoolTail-shaped groups in offloading scheduler
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
Follow-up to #55034 (divisibility-assert fix — required; offloading a KpoolTail group crashes without it). With that landed, GLM5Next (KDA+MLA hybrid with a `KpoolTail` scratch group) boots with native KV offloading but then crashes at **three later points** in the offloading scheduler, all rooted in the same shape: the KpoolTail group has `tokens_per_chunk=4 < tokens_per_hash=16`, so it resolves to `hashes_per_chunk == 0` and carries no hash-addressable offload blocks by construction.

1. `update_offload_keys()`: `islice(step=0)` raises `ValueError: Indices for islice() must be None or an integer` on the first scheduled request.
2. `storable_chunks()`: `tokens_per_chunk <= 0` must return 0 chunks (also guards the division).
3. `_build_store_jobs()`: `offload_keys` for the zero-chunk group are never appended while `offload_block_ids` positions advance via the shared hybrid allocator → `assert len(offload_keys) == len(offload_block_ids)`.

## Changes
- Skip groups with `hashes_per_chunk <= 0` in `update_offload_keys()`.
- Guard `storable_chunks()` against `tokens_per_chunk <= 0`.
- Skip zero-chunk groups in `_build_store_jobs()`; cap `offload_block_ids` by the `offload_keys` length so the two stay consistent by construction.
- Regression tests for each guard in `tests/v1/offloading/`.

## Why the assert fix and these guards are separate PRs
PR #55034 (assert) is the smallest, cleanest bug and is independently reviewable. These scheduler guards only matter once a KpoolTail group is actually scheduled with offloading enabled — they build on the assert fix.

title: [Bugfix][CI] Set cudagraph_mode=FULL for the Ernie4.5-VL ViT cudagraph test
bodyExcerpt:
Ernie4.5-VL ViT cudagraph test fails after #54782

Failing test: `test_vit_cudagraph_image[ernie45_vl]`

AMD CI: <https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12553/list?sid=01a0615a-019d-4492-a92c-a4018dfdcc8b&tab=output>

**The same group failed on both MI300 and MI355.**

## Error

```
RuntimeError: Ernie4_5_VLMoeForConditionalGeneration: piecewise CUDA graphs
(cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) unavailable, model is not torch-compiled
and breakable CUDA graph is off. Set VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 or
cudagraph_mode=NONE/FULL.
```

Raised in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`, during engine start.

## What exposed it

`1c26e57d3c` — [Bugfix] Raise for unavailable piecewise CUDA graphs (#54782).
It added a guard that raises when piecewise cudagraphs are requested for a
model with no active `@support_torch_compile` wrapper.

## Root cause

The guard is correct; the misconfiguration predates it. `Ernie4_5_VLMoeModel`
keeps its `@support_torch_compile` decorator commented out, since the model
was added in #22514:

```python
# Since Ernie VL distinguishes between text experts and vision experts,
# enabling torch.compile will cause errors.
# @support_torch_compile(
```

So the model is not compiled, piecewise cudagraphs have nothing to partition,
and the test asks for the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Until #54782 this
silently captured nothing.

Not platform-specific: `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` defaults to `False`
everywhere and the test is gated on `is_cuda_alike()`, so CUDA should hit it
too.

Ernie is the only affected model in that file — `glm4_1v` and `step3_vl` pass,
and `deepseek_ocr` already pins `cudagraph_mode`.

## Fix

Pin the mode for the Ernie entry, the way `deepseek_ocr` in the same file
already does:

```python
compilation_config_overrides={
    "cudagraph_mode": 2,  # FULL
},
```

Verified on MI300X: fails in 31s before, passes in 40s after.

title: [Bug] modelopt NVFP4 MoE: mismatched w1/w3 global scales are detected, warned about, and then used anyway
bodyExcerpt:
### The behaviour

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.process_weights_after_loading` fuses `gate_proj` and `up_proj` into `w13` and keeps only the **gate** per-tensor global scale:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L967-L975

```python
# Use a single gscale for w13.
if self.moe.is_act_and_mul and not torch.allclose(
    layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0], layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 1]
):
    logger.warning_once(
        "w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected."
    )
w13_weight_scale_2 = layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0].contiguous()
```

When the two differ, the up-projection half of `w13` is then dequantised with the gate half's global scale. The mismatch is detected, logged once, and the wrong scale is used anyway.

### How far apart they can be

Measured directly from the checkpoints on disk (reading only the `weight_scale_2` scalars — no GPU, no inference):

| checkpoint | modelopt | gate/up pairs | pairs that differ | ratio median / p99 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4` | 0.45.0 | 12,384 | **8,563 (69.1%)** | 1.077 / 1.69 / **10.0** |
| `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 0.46.0 | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |
| `mazinb/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-NVFP4` | 0.46.0-compatible-rtn | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |

All 43 MoE layers of the GLM checkpoint are affected; the worst layer has 272 of 288 experts mismatched. So this is not universal — the two modelopt 0.46 checkpoints tie the two scales exactly — but when a checkpoint does not tie them, the divergence is large and the whole model is affected.

title: [CI][Spec Decode] Add MTP placeholder-token regression coverage
bodyExcerpt:
- Add a focused MTP regression test that compares emitted token IDs with a non-speculative greedy baseline.
- Exercise both `PIECEWISE` and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graph modes and verify that the requested mode is not silently downgraded.
- Force deterministic draft rejection with a nonzero allowed token ID so any leaked placeholder slots are immediately observable as an output mismatch.
- Assert that the MTP drafter produced drafts and accepted none, while also exercising the logprobs output-assembly path.

Speculative decoding is an exact optimization at temperature zero, so its emitted token IDs must match ordinary greedy decoding token for token. A previous MTP regression under FULL CUDA graphs instead exposed the complete padded speculative width rather than truncating it to the accepted prefix. Rejected positions use a placeholder token ID, which is converted to token ID 0 before logprob gathering and can therefore become silent output corruption if padded positions escape the output-assembly boundary. With the GLM-5.1 tokenizer, token ID 0 renders as `!`, producing responses filled with repeated exclamation marks. The engine continued running normally and reported healthy acceptance statistics, so liveness checks and acceptance-rate tests could not detect the problem. PIECEWISE execution also remained correct, meaning coverage that does not explicitly exercise a FULL graph mode can miss the regression. Comparing emitted token IDs in both graph modes, while proving that rejection actually occurred, provides a deterministic and tokenizer-independent guard for this defect class.

AI assistance was used for duplicate research, test design, implementation, validation, and PR preparation. The human submitter reviewed the resulting change and remains responsible for it end to end.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3 reasoning leaks into content when clients pass enable_thinking/thinking=false — parser gates on kwargs the GLM-5.3 template never reads
bodyExcerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

GLM-5.3's chat template has **no thinking on/off switch** — its only knobs are `reasoning_effort` (`'low'`/`'high'`, anything else → `'max'`) and `clear_thinking`:

```jinja2
{%- set effective_reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort if reasoning_effort is defined and reasoning_effort in ['low', 'high'] else 'max' -%}
```

(`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` `chat_template.jinja`; `enable_thinking` appears nowhere in the template.)

But the GLM reasoning parser still gates reasoning **extraction** on the GLM-4.5/4.6-era kwargs. At current `main`, `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py`:

```python
chat_kwargs = kwargs.get("chat_template_kwargs", {}) or {}
thinking = chat_kwargs.get("thinking", None)
enable_thinking = chat_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", None)
self.thinking_enabled = (
    True
    if thinking is None and enable_thinking is None
    else bool(thinking) or bool(enable_thinking)
)
```

So when a client sends `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` — the documented way to disable thinking on GLM-4.5/4.6, which many clients still send to anything GLM-shaped — the two halves disagree:

- **Template**: unchanged (the variable is never read) → the model thinks anyway.
- **Parser**: `thinking_enabled = False` → extraction off.

Result: the raw scratchpad plus a dangling `</think>` land in `message.content`:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Simple question.</think>2 + 2 = **4**\n\nIs there anything else you'd like help with?"}
```

The same request without the kwarg returns clean `content` with the thought in `reasoning`. Verified live (GLM-5.3-Flash, `--reasoning-parser glm45` on a fork tracking base `55969c16`; the gating logic above is unchanged at current `main`, though I could not runtime-test `main` on this hardware).

### Repro

```bash
# leak: scratchpad + </think> in content
curl $HOST/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{
  "model": "GLM-5.3-Flash", "max_tokens": 60,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": fa

title: [Bug]: `MooncakeStoreScheduler` fatal assert "Missing current block table for store request" when a KV load failure recovery (#19330) reschedules the request
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

**Component:** `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py` (`_apply_current_save_block_ids`), interplay between #51358 and #19330.

**Environment:** vLLM main (v0.28.1rc1.dev), GLM-4.7/5.x fp8 MLA, TP8/DCP4, `MooncakeStoreConnector` with async KV loads + KV load failure recovery (`recompute`/`reschedule` policy).

### 🐛 Describe the bug



## Symptom

EngineCore dies with:

```
AssertionError: Missing current block table for store request chatcmpl-xxx
  in _apply_current_save_block_ids (mooncake/store/scheduler.py)
```

The assert fires when the Mooncake store has a degraded moment (SSD read failures `BUFFER_OVERFLOW`, transfer `-200`/`-800`), which triggers the KV load failure recovery path. Every such incident is a hard EngineCore crash (all in-flight requests 500).

## Root cause

Two merged upstream features establish an invariant that is violated under load failure:

1. **#51358** ([Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states) added the defensive invariant in `_apply_current_save_block_ids`: every request whose ReqMeta has `can_save=True` must have a current block table present in `scheduler_output.kv_connector_block_state.block_ids`.
2. **#19330** ([V1][P/D] Add Support for KV Load Failure Recovery) lets the scheduler reschedule a request after an async KV load failure (`failed_recving_kv_req_ids`, request moved back to WAITING, blocks freed/cached).

`kv_connector_block_state.block_ids` only snapshots requests **scheduled this step** (new reqs + cached reqs with new blocks + boundary-state offloads). A request recovering from a load failure can end that step outside the snapshot while a `can_save=True` ReqMeta is still produced (e.g. via the pending-load branch when `can_load` was re-enabled by a retried lookup, or the scheduled-producer branch whose blocks were concurrently released). The assert then fires and kills EngineCore.

This is not specific to Mamba/GLM: any Mooncake Store deployme

title: [Bug]: AITER topK meta buffer ignores pcp_size — every PCP start fails with fused shared experts on ROCm
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

8x AMD MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, AITER, GLM-5.3-Flash (MoE with fused shared experts).

### Describe the bug

`_init_aiter_shared_experts_topK_buffer()` sizes the AITER topK metadata buffer
with `max_num_batched_tokens * dp_size` but ignores `pcp_size`, so **every** start
with `--prefill-context-parallel-size > 1` aborts during warmup when
`num_fused_shared_experts > 0` on ROCm.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/expert_map_manager.py#L258-L269

```python
def _init_aiter_shared_experts_topK_buffer(self):
    if self.num_fused_shared_experts > 0:
        dp_size = self.moe_parallel_config.dp_size
        init_aiter_topK_meta_data(
            ...
            max_num_tokens=self.max_num_batched_tokens * dp_size,   # <- no pcp_size
        )
```

Under PCP the MoE sees the tokens gathered across the PCP ranks, so the actual
token count is `max_num_batched_tokens * pcp_size`. The comment on the EPLB check
in `config/parallel.py` states this directly:

> The EP group spans the TP x PCP x DP ranks.

`pcp_size` is already a field of `FusedMoEParallelConfig`, right next to `dp_size`.

### Reproduction

`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, otherwise unchanged:

```
--prefill-context-parallel-size 2
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'AITER topK meta data support 32768 tokens
which is determined by max_num_batched_tokens, but got 65536 tokens now.'

--prefill-context-parallel-size 4
... but got 131072 tokens now.
```

Exactly `32768 * pcp_size` in both cases.

### Suggested fix

```python
dp_size = self.moe_parallel_config.dp_size
pcp_size = self.moe_parallel_config.pcp_size
init_aiter_topK_meta_data(
    ...
    max_num_tokens=self.max_num_batched_tokens * dp_size * pcp_size,
)
```

The buffer is `(max_num_tokens, top_k + n_shared + is_EP)` in fp32 plus an int32
twin, so even at `pcp_size=4` this is a few MB. The assert is `>=`, so
over-allocating is harmless.

### Scope of what I verified

V
